clickup_spec.behaviour: A persistent search field sits in the centre of the workspace top bar. Clicking it opens a full search modal that overlays the page. The keyboard shortcut is shown inline in the field itself.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Field shows a magnifier icon, the word "Search", and a grey keycap hint "Ctrl K" to its right. Immediately to the right of the field, outside it, is a separate pill "AI Chats" with a multicolour sparkle glyph.

clickup_spec.behaviour: The modal is a large centred panel. Row 1 = the query text (very large type) with a clear "×" and an "Ask AI" pill on the right. Row 2 = cross-app source tabs. Row 3 = entity-type chips + Filter + Sort. Then the result body. Then a keyboard-hint footer.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Query rendered at ~24px with a visible caret. Right of the query: "×" then a pill labelled "Ask AI" with a sparkle glyph. Footer: "‹" "›" arrows, then the sentence "Press [/] to see all available commands, hit [Tab] to see additional actions" ("/" and "Tab" rendered as key badges), and a gear icon flush right.

clickup_spec.behaviour: While typing, a small floating bubble appears above the modal offering shorter/prefix completions of the typed string as clickable chips.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Dark rounded bubble, chips "vn" and "vnjf" side by side, positioned above and left of the query row.

clickup_spec.behaviour: A tab strip scopes the search to a connected source. "All" is the default and is underlined when active. Selecting a source restricts results to that provider.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Tabs in order, each with its vendor logo: "All" (no logo, active/underlined) | "ClickUp" | "Google Drive" | "Gmail" | "SharePoint" | "Apps" (grid glyph).

clickup_spec.behaviour: A row of rounded pills narrows results to one or more entity types. Clicking a chip selects it (fills it grey); clicking the same chip again unselects it. Multiple chips can be selected at once. Each selected chip counts toward the Filter chip's badge count.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Default visible chips, each with a leading icon: "Tasks" (check-circle), "Docs" (page), "Agents" (goggles), "Channels" (#), "Messages" (speech bubble). Selected state = filled grey background (transcript: "yeh GRAY COLOR ho gaya"). Unselected = outline only. Then a "⋯" overflow chip, a vertical divider, then "Filter" and "Sort".

clickup_spec.behaviour: The "⋯" chip opens a dropdown that lets the user choose WHICH entity types appear as chips in the row. Types are split into "Shown" and "Hidden"; ticking a Hidden type promotes it into the visible chip row (and it can then be selected as a filter). The list is searchable.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Dropdown contains: search input with magnifier, placeholder "Search..."; section header "Shown" (checked blue checkboxes, e.g. "Messages"); section header "Hidden" with unchecked checkboxes for, in alphabetical order: "Clips", "Comments", "Dashboards", "Files", "Folders", "Forms", "Lists", "People", "Spaces". Checkbox is on the RIGHT of each row, icon on the left. Panel scrolls.

clickup_spec.behaviour: The "Filter" chip opens a dropdown of filter rows. Each row shows its current value inline and a "›" that opens a submenu picker. The Filter chip's label changes from "Filter" to "N Filter" once anything is active, and the chip fills grey.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Panel label "Filters". Rows in exact order: "Assignee" — "Anyone" ›; "Creator" — "Anyone" ›; "Location" — "Any" ›; "Status" — "Any" ›; "Task types" — "Any" ›; "Archived" — toggle switch (default OFF). Chip reads "1 Filter" with a funnel icon once one is applied.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Both open a searchable people picker submenu that renders to the left of the filter panel. Creator = who made the item; Assignee = who the item was given to (transcript [02:25]: managers create tasks, team members do the work).
clickup_spec.ui_details: Submenu: search input with magnifier, placeholder "Search...", then avatar + display-name rows — "Hamda Tahir", "suleman". Default value on both rows is "Anyone".

clickup_spec.behaviour: Scopes the search to a container — "kis space mein para hai, ya kis list mein para hai". Offers shortcuts for where the user currently is, plus a browsable tree of spaces. Multi-select via checkboxes.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Submenu: search input with magnifier, placeholder "Search..."; section header "Suggested" → "Current location" (map-pin icon) + checkbox, "Personal List" (person-list icon) + checkbox; section header "Browse" → "Space" (blue S square) + checkbox, "Team Space" + checkbox. Checkboxes on the right. Default value in the parent row is "Any".

clickup_spec.behaviour: Narrows to task state — per transcript [02:56] the meaning is "either the task is ACTIVE or it is CLOSED".
clickup_spec.ui_details: Row "Status" with a circle icon, current value "Any", chevron "›" to a submenu.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Narrows to a workspace-defined task type (Task / Milestone / custom types).
clickup_spec.ui_details: Row "Task types" with a tag icon, current value "Any", chevron "›".

clickup_spec.behaviour: A binary switch, not a value picker — flipping it on includes archived items in the results.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Row "Archived" with a box icon; a pill toggle switch on the right, default OFF (grey, knob left).

clickup_spec.behaviour: A separate chip next to Filter that reorders the result set.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Chip labelled "Sort" with an up/down chevron glyph, sitting immediately right of the Filter chip.

clickup_spec.feature: AI fallback answer on zero results
clickup_spec.behaviour: When the text query matches nothing, the modal does NOT show a dead empty state. It automatically hands the query to the AI ("Brain"), streams a visible reasoning trace, then renders a conversational answer inline in the result area, with feedback controls and a hand-off into a full AI chat.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Header line: "No exact matches found, but here's a relevant answer from ✦ Brain". Streaming trace lines with animated dots, e.g. "Reasoning …", "Checking what \"vnjfv\" points to …", "Checking whether \"vnjfv\" is a known term …" / "Pondering …", "Checking if \"vnjfv\" matches anything in ClickUp …", "Checking whether \"vnjfv\" means anything …". Answer text e.g. "Looks like a typo, Hamda. What were you trying to say?". Action row under the answer: copy icon, thumbs-up, thumbs-down (left); "✦ Continue with Brain" (right). The reasoning re-runs when the chip selection changes.

clickup_spec.behaviour: A persistent button in the modal header sends the current query straight to the AI regardless of whether results exist.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Pill labelled "Ask AI" with a multicolour sparkle glyph, top-right of the query row, immediately right of the "×" clear button.

clickup_spec.behaviour: The modal advertises its own keys: "/" switches into a command list, "Tab" opens per-result actions. Prev/next arrows page the result set. A gear opens search settings.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Footer: "‹" "›" then "Press [/] to see all available commands, hit [Tab] to see additional actions", gear icon flush right.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Per transcript [01:15]: a user can only search within the access they have been granted — results never expose items outside their permission scope.
clickup_spec.ui_details: No dedicated UI; enforced server-side on the result set.

gaps.title: Command palette chunk fails to load and takes the whole app down
gaps.ask: "Agar Rundex search mein open karein to yahan pe bhi ek search bar hai… Filhaal is feature ka masla hai — I don't know kya" — she opens our search, the app dies, and she moves on to ClickUp.
gaps.why: Frame 015_0101 is our own RouteErrorBoundary filling the viewport: "Something went wrong / Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: https://rundesk.theaura.agency/assets/command-palette-NaNmjPLK.js / Try again / Go home". apps/web/src/routes/app.tsx:8-11 lazy-imports the palette with no retry and no error boundary of its own; the `<Suspense fallback={null}>` at app.tsx:131-140 catches the pending state but not a rejected import, so the throw escapes to the root errorComponent and blanks the entire shell — sidebar, top bar and current page all gone. The hash in the filename says this is the classic stale-index-after-deploy failure: the browser holds an old index.html pointing at a chunk that no longer exists. Two fixes belong together: retry the dynamic import once and hard-reload on a second failure, and wrap the palette in a local boundary so a chunk miss degrades to "search unavailable" instead of destroying the app. Highest-priority item in this section — every other search gap is invisible while search itself cannot open.

gaps.title: Location filter — scope search to a space, folder or list
gaps.ask: "LOCATION ka matlab yeh hota hai ke woh kis space mein para hai, ya kis list mein para hai."
gaps.why: ClickUp's filter panel has "Location — Any ›" opening a picker with a "Search..." box, a "Suggested" section ("Current location", "Personal List") and a "Browse" section ("Space", "Team Space"), all multi-select checkboxes (frame 045_0250). We have no equivalent: SearchFilters (apps/api/src/modules/search/search.service.ts:33-60) has no location field, the controller accepts no such param, and the palette has no control. The indexing side is already done — every Meili doc carries listId and spaceId (search.service.ts:78-79, 134-147) and both are declared filterable at search.service.ts:122 — so this is wiring a filter through an index that already supports it, plus the Postgres branch joins that already reach spaces/projects/lists (search.service.ts:399-405). "Current location" is the highest-value part: search inside the space I am looking at.

gaps.title: Folders (and Lists / Spaces) are not searchable entity types

gaps.why: She picks Folders specifically and it becomes a chip she can search by (frames 035_0203 → 040_0225). Our searchable set is fixed at apps/api/src/modules/search/search.controller.ts:11 — task, doc, file, user, comment, channel, message — and folders are a real container in our product (packages/db/src/schema/folders.ts, apps/api/src/modules/folders/folders.service.ts:17) that search simply never queries. Same for lists and spaces/projects. Add a name-search branch per container type in SearchService (with the existing folderVisibilityFilter from apps/api/src/common/permissions/item-visibility applied, the way tasks already use taskVisibilityFilter), extend ENTITY_TYPES/ENTITY_ORDER, add icons and i18n labels.

clickup_spec.feature: Branded app-shell skeleton on cold load (never a blank screen)
clickup_spec.behaviour: From the moment the HTML paints until the workspace data lands, ClickUp renders the full app chrome as gray placeholder shapes plus an animated brand logo. The user never sees an empty viewport: even at t=0 the top bar, the left icon rail and the bottom status bar are drawn as blocks in their final positions, so the layout does not jump when real content arrives. The shell survives a URL change (/team-invite → /signup) without flashing to blank.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Top bar placeholders: one ~130×28 light-gray rounded rect at far left (workspace name), one ~320×30 rounded pill horizontally centred (global search), three ~24×24 rounded squares + one ~28px circle at far right (icon buttons + avatar). Left edge: one solid dark rounded vertical strip, full height, the width of the icon rail. Content pane: plain white. Dead centre of the content pane: the ClickUp logo mark, animating (chevron + swoosh), roughly 64px. Bottom of the content pane: three rounded pill placeholders in a row, widths short / long / medium, left-aligned. Zero text strings are rendered anywhere during this phase. In the earliest frame the previously-known workspace name ('T  The AURA AGENCY ⌄') is still painted in the chip position before it degrades to a placeholder — i.e. cached identity shows first, then the placeholder.

clickup_spec.feature: Per-card skeleton rows — chrome first, each widget resolves independently
clickup_spec.behaviour: Once the shell is real, ClickUp paints every piece of navigation and every card header immediately and fills only the *data* regions with skeleton rows. Cards resolve independently: on the same screen 'Recent' and 'Docs' are still showing skeleton rows while 'Bookmarks' and 'Folders' have already resolved to their empty states. The skeleton rows mirror the shape of the real row (icon + title), and the card's scrollbar is already sized, so nothing reflows on arrival.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Skeleton row = a ~24×24 light-gray rounded square at the left gutter + a full-width light-gray rounded bar ~14px tall for the title, repeated 8+ times down the card with even vertical spacing. Rows shimmer at slightly different intensities (travelling gradient). Card title ('Recent', 'Docs') is real text at the top-left of the card from the first paint. Each card keeps its own vertical scrollbar with up/down carets visible while skeleton. Sidebar, icon rail, view tabs, Filters and the Refreshed/Auto refresh/Customize/Add card toolbar are all fully rendered while the cards are still skeleton.

clickup_spec.feature: Loaded-empty is visually distinct from still-loading
clickup_spec.behaviour: A card that has finished loading with no data does not fall back to a spinner or a bare line of text — it shows an illustrated empty state with an explanatory sentence and a primary action, so the user can tell 'nothing here yet' apart from 'still fetching'.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Bookmarks card empty state: large outlined bookmark-ribbon glyph with a small '+' badge at its lower-right, body copy 'Bookmarks make it easy to save ClickUp items or any URL from around the web.', black filled button 'Add Bookmark'. Folders card empty state: large outlined folder glyph, caption 'Add new Folder to your Space', black filled button 'Add Folder'. Both are centred within the card, icon → text → button, stacked.

clickup_spec.feature: Invite acceptance screen with an explicit decline path
clickup_spec.behaviour: An invitee opening the emailed link lands on a standalone, unauthenticated confirmation screen naming the workspace and the inviter (with the inviter's email address in parentheses), and is asked to confirm before being dropped into the workspace. Accepting is the primary action; declining is offered as an equal-weight but visually secondary text action directly beneath it. A help affordance sits at the bottom of the page.
clickup_spec.ui_details: URL /join-team?email=…&token=…. Layout is a single centred column on a pastel gradient wash (pink/lavender/peach at the top fading to white), no sidebar or app chrome. Order: ClickUp logo mark → heading 'Join the Leo Workspace on ClickUp' (workspace name interpolated into the heading itself) → sub-line 'Invited by suleman (sulemanabad214@gmail.com)' → full-width black rounded primary button 'Accept invite' → plain dark text link 'Decline invite' immediately below with no button chrome → far down the page, a small centred link 'Need help?'.

clickup_spec.feature: Freshness + refresh chrome on an Overview surface
clickup_spec.behaviour: The Overview view tells the user how stale the data is and whether it is refreshing itself, and lets them recompose the surface, all from the same toolbar row as the filters.

clickup_spec.feature: Task types (what a task IS) as a first-class attribute
clickup_spec.behaviour: ClickUp models a task's *type* separately from its status. A type answers "what is this row" — Task, Milestone, Campaign, Invoice — while status answers "what state is it in". The consultant's argument (03:04-03:45): a piece of work spanning a month / 22-23 working days cannot honestly be called a "task"; it is a MILESTONE, and the type label is what gives any team member CLARITY about the time horizon of the row they are looking at. Because the type is a real attribute it is (a) selectable when the task is created, and (b) a filter dimension in global search.
clickup_spec.ui_details: In the search Filters popover the row reads exactly "Task types" with a value column reading "Any" and a right-pointing chevron ">" that opens a submenu. It sits between "Status" and "Archived" in the list. Transcript at 03:00-03:04 pairs it with STATUS as the two things you get "jab search mein jaate hain".

clickup_spec.behaviour: The "Filter" button in the search modal opens a popover panel headed "Filters" listing six filter dimensions. Five are drill-down rows (label on the left, current value in the middle, chevron on the right) and one is an inline toggle. Default value for every drill-down is "Anyone" (people) or "Any" (everything else), i.e. unfiltered.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Panel title "Filters". Rows top-to-bottom with their icons: person icon "Assignee — Anyone >"; person icon "Creator — Anyone >"; folder icon "Location — Any >"; circle icon "Status — Any >"; card icon "Task types — Any >"; archive-box icon "Archived — [toggle, off]". Hovering a row highlights it (Status row is highlighted in 047/052). The popover is anchored under the "Filter" button, to the left of "Sort".

clickup_spec.behaviour: Clicking the "Status" row opens a submenu to the LEFT of the Filters panel offering three mutually-exclusive choices, with the current one check-marked. "All" is the default and is explicitly offered as an option rather than being implied by deselection.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Submenu items, top to bottom: "All" with a ✓ on the right, "Active", "Closed". Rendered as a separate floating card that overlaps the search results area.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Archived items are excluded from search by default; a single toggle in the Filters panel brings them back into the result set. Transcript 03:52: "agar hum ne koi cheez ARCHIVE ki to woh bhi show aati hai" — i.e. once flipped on, archived things surface in the same result list.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Row label "Archived" with an archive-box icon; control is an iOS-style pill toggle rendered in the off/grey position on the right of the row. No chevron — it toggles in place, it does not open a submenu.

clickup_spec.behaviour: The "Sort" button (right of "Filter") opens a five-item dropdown. Relevance is the default and is check-marked. Two options are timestamp-based, which is the date-oriented search the consultant describes at 04:00 ("last created date kya thi — dates ke lehaz par"). Two more are engagement-based ranking modes computed from workspace and personal activity.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Dropdown items top-to-bottom: "Relevance" (rendered in purple/active with a ✓ at the far right), "Last Updated", "Last Created", "Trending In Workspace", "Trending For You". Menu is anchored under the Sort button and overlays the result area.

clickup_spec.feature: Federated search across connected external apps
clickup_spec.behaviour: The search modal's first row is a source picker: search runs across ClickUp's own data AND connected third-party accounts, so one query returns Drive files and Gmail threads alongside tasks and docs. Transcript 04:04-04:26: Google Drive is not part of ClickUp, it is an outsourced/outer part, but you LINK it to your ClickUp and then searching from the search bar also finds things out of your Google Drive — "yeh ClickUp ki quality hai ke woh apni workspace ko itna BROADER mein le ke jaa raha hai". Sources not yet connected show a "+" affordance to connect them. Each source has a keyboard shortcut for jumping straight to it.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Tab row directly under the query input, left to right: "All" (active, underlined), "ClickUp" (with ClickUp logo), "Google Drive" (Drive logo with a small "+" badge), "Gmail" (Gmail logo with "+" badge), "SharePoint" (SharePoint logo with "+" badge), "Apps" (grid icon). Hovering "Google Drive" shows a dark tooltip reading "Filter by Google Drive" with two key caps "Ctrl" and "3" — so the sources are ordered and keyboard-addressable (Ctrl+1..n).

clickup_spec.behaviour: A second row of chips narrows results by ClickUp object type, independently of the source tabs and of the Filters popover.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Chips left to right: "Tasks" (check-circle icon), "Docs" (doc icon), "Agents" (glasses icon), "# Channels", "Folders" (folder icon), then a "⋯" overflow chip. To their right, separated by a divider: "Filter" (funnel icon) and "Sort" (up-down arrows icon).

clickup_spec.feature: AI fallback when search finds nothing
clickup_spec.behaviour: A zero-result query does not dead-end. ClickUp Brain answers inline inside the same modal, addresses the user by name, and offers to continue the conversation.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Result area reads "No exact matches found, but here's a relevant answer from ✨ Brain" (Brain is a coloured link), then the answer body "That looks like a typo, Hamda. What did you mean?". Below the answer: copy icon, thumbs-up icon, thumbs-down icon on the left; "✨ Continue with Brain" on the right. Top-right of the query row carries an "X" clear button and an "Ask AI ✨" button.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Persistent footer teaches the keyboard surface of the palette.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Left: "‹" and "›" pager arrows. Then "Press [ / ] to see all available commands, hit [ Tab ] to see additional actions" with "/" and "Tab" rendered as key caps. Far right: a gear icon (search settings).

She wants to pick Task vs Milestone (vs Campaign etc.) at the moment the task is created, not afterwards.
gaps.why: Frame 058_0340 shows the Rundesk Create modal with only: Task title, Space, Project, List, Cancel, Create task. The web form posts `{ listId, title, priority: 'normal' }` (quick-create-modal.tsx:164). Worse, the gap is not UI-only as it first appears: `CreateTaskDto` (dto/task.dto.ts:18-67) has no `taskTypeId` field and the global whitelist ValidationPipe would strip it, and `tasks.controller.ts:107-126` never forwards one to `createTask`. The service parameter exists and is honoured (tasks.service.ts:1459, 1480) but is unreachable from HTTP — today a new task can ONLY receive the workspace default type via `defaultTaskTypeForList` (tasks.service.ts:1383-1393). Choosing a non-default type requires a second round-trip to `PATCH /tasks/:taskId/task-type`. Same is true of `isMilestone`, which is only settable on PATCH (tasks.controller.ts:144).

gaps.title: Task types are invisible in a fresh workspace — no seeded Task/Milestone and the picker self-hides at zero types
gaps.ask: Her whole argument is that a member must be able to see at a glance whether a row is a same-day task or a month-long MILESTONE. That only works if the vocabulary exists out of the box.
gaps.why: Nothing seeds task types: migration `packages/db/src/migrations/0091_task_types_reporting_and_workdays.sql` creates the table only, and there is no insert in the sample-data module. Meanwhile `TaskTypePicker` bails out with `if (types.length === 0) return null` (task-detail-sheet.tsx:416), so a brand-new workspace shows no picker anywhere and nothing signposts Settings → Task types. The built feature is effectively dark. Seed at least "Task" (isDefault true) and "Milestone" per workspace on creation — note `uq_task_types_one_default` allows exactly one default (task-types.ts:30).

gaps.title: Search cannot filter by task type
gaps.ask: Frames 047/052/061 show "Task types — Any >" as a first-class row in ClickUp's search Filters panel, sitting right beside Status — and she opens the section at 03:00 by naming exactly those two: "yeh do cheezein hain: STATUS aur TASK TYPE".
gaps.why: `SearchFilters` (search.service.ts:33-60) has no `taskTypeId`; `search.controller.ts:25-77` accepts types/statusCategory/priority/assigneeId/creatorId/includeArchived/labelId/dueAfter/dueBefore/customFieldId/customFieldValue/sort and nothing else; the palette's filter panel (command-palette.tsx:402-556) renders Type, Sort, Status, Priority, Label, Assignee, Creator, Archived, Due, Custom field — no task-type control. The column `tasks.task_type_id` and its index `tasks_task_type_idx` already exist (schema/tasks.ts:42, 66), so this is a join + one param + one chip group.

gaps.title: Search has no Location filter — every query is workspace-wide
gaps.ask: ClickUp's Filters panel offers "Location — Any >" (frames 047/052/061) to scope a search to a space, folder or list.
gaps.why: Rundesk search always spans the whole workspace: `search.service.ts:313` builds the Meili filter as `[\`workspaceId = "..."\`]` and nothing ever adds a space or list clause, even though `listId` and `spaceId` are already declared filterable on the index (search.service.ts:122) and are already written into every indexed doc (search.service.ts:132-149). The controller exposes no spaceId/projectId/listId param. Cheap to add on the Meili path; the Postgres fallback branches need the space/project/list joins they already perform for URL construction.

gaps.title: No federated search across connected apps — Google Drive results never appear in the palette
gaps.ask: "GOOGLE DRIVE ClickUp ka part nahi hai — woh ek outsourced / outer part hai... Lekin hum is ko LINK kar sakte hain apne ClickUp ke saath. Agar hum Google Drive se search karenge to woh humari Google Drive se bhi cheezein dhoond ke mila ke de sakta hai. Yeh ClickUp ki quality hai ke woh apni workspace ko itna BROADER mein le ke jaa raha hai." Then, flatly: "Ab yeh maine aap ko sirf abhi search bar ka bataya, jo ke humare end par MISSING POINT hai — ke search bar ka vision humare end par kya hona chahiye."
gaps.why: Rundesk search knows seven entity types, all internal: 'task' | 'doc' | 'file' | 'user' | 'comment' | 'channel' | 'message' (search.service.ts:18). The 'file' branch reads only task attachments (search.service.ts:610-634) and R2-hosted clips (search.service.ts:644-675). There is no Drive/Gmail/SharePoint source tab, no per-source keyboard shortcut, no "+" connect affordance. Drive itself IS connected-capable — `google-drive` is a supported OAuth provider (integration-connections.service.ts:84) with token refresh, and tasks can attach and preview Drive files (tasks.service.ts:962-963, 1066; task-detail-sheet.tsx:1719-2003) — but the granted scope is `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` (integration-connections.service.ts:467), which only reaches files the app created or the user explicitly picked. Drive-wide search needs `drive.readonly` (or `drive.metadata.readonly`), a re-consent path for already-connected workspaces, a files.list proxy endpoint, and the source-tab UI in the palette.

gaps.title: No engagement-based sort modes (Trending In Workspace / Trending For You)
gaps.ask: ClickUp's Sort menu (frame 066_0412) offers five modes; Rundesk implements three of them.
gaps.why: Rundesk has Relevance / Last updated / Last created (command-palette.tsx:412-422, catalogs.ts:4614-4617, meiliSort at search.service.ts:86-90) and nothing else — a case-insensitive grep for "trending" across apps and packages returns only the `TrendingUp` lucide icon in dashboard/report builders. Real trending needs view/open telemetry per object per user, which Rundesk does not currently record for search targets. Lowest-value item in this section; listed for completeness, not urgency.

gaps.title: Date filtering in search covers due dates only — no created/updated range
gaps.ask: "yahan se bhi hum log search kar sakte hain ke abhi hua tha yeh — last created date kya thi — dates ke lehaz par."
gaps.why: Partially covered: sorting by Last created and Last updated both work (command-palette.tsx:412-422; controller accepts sort=created|updated at search.controller.ts:62). What is absent is a created-date or updated-date *range* — the only date range in the palette is `dueAfter` → `dueBefore` (command-palette.tsx:498-514; search.controller.ts:38-39), i.e. when work is due, not when it was made. `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are already indexed and sortable in Meili (search.service.ts:122) so a range clause is inexpensive.

gaps.title: Task type is never shown on a task row — only inside the detail sheet
gaps.ask: Her stated purpose for types is at-a-glance CLARITY "kisi bhi member ko" about a row's time horizon. That requires the badge to be on the row, not two clicks deep.
gaps.why: `TaskTypePicker` renders only in the task detail sheet (task-detail-sheet.tsx:387-436, mounted at :708). Grepping `taskType` across `apps/web/src/routes/app.$workspaceId.$spaceId.$projectId.$listId.tsx` returns nothing — list rows, board cards and subtask rows carry no type badge, no type column and no group-by-type. Contrast the milestone flag, which IS surfaced on rows as an amber diamond (listId route :2665, :3126; workspace-timeline-page.tsx:447, 463). The API already returns the joined `taskType` object with icon and colour on task detail (tasks.service.ts:2000-2004); the list endpoint would need it added.

gaps.title: Status filter has no explicit "All" chip
gaps.ask: ClickUp's Status submenu (frames 047/052) lists "All ✓ / Active / Closed" — All is a visible, check-marked default.
gaps.why: Rundesk renders three toggle chips — To do / Active / Closed (command-palette.tsx:423-433, catalogs.ts:3290-3292) — where clearing the filter means clicking the active chip a second time to deselect it. The Type filter group right above it DOES have an explicit "All" chip (command-palette.tsx:403-405), so the palette is internally inconsistent as well as divergent from ClickUp. Cosmetic, one chip.

rundesk_status.feature: Choosing a task type at creation time
rundesk_status.evidence: apps/web/src/components/quick-create-modal.tsx:135-201 — TaskForm posts `{ listId, title, priority: 'normal' }` (line 164) with no type control; apps/api/src/modules/tasks/dto/task.dto.ts:18-67 CreateTaskDto has no `taskTypeId`; apps/api/src/modules/tasks/tasks.controller.ts:107-126 never forwards one
rundesk_status.notes: Not merely a UI gap. `tasks.service.ts:1459` declares `taskTypeId?` and :1480 honours it, but no HTTP route can supply it — the whitelist ValidationPipe strips unknown body keys. In practice a new task can only inherit the workspace default via `defaultTaskTypeForList` (tasks.service.ts:1383-1393); anything else needs a second call to PATCH /tasks/:taskId/task-type.

rundesk_status.evidence: not found after searching packages/db/src (only schema/tasks.ts references taskTypes), apps/api/src/modules/sample-data, and migration 0091_task_types_reporting_and_workdays.sql — no INSERT into task_types anywhere
rundesk_status.notes: Every workspace starts with an empty vocabulary. Combined with the picker's zero-length early return, the whole feature is dark until an admin finds Settings → Task types unprompted.

rundesk_status.evidence: packages/db/src/schema/tasks.ts:37-39 `isMilestone` boolean; toggle in apps/web/src/components/task-detail-sheet.tsx:540-541 and :815-824 (Diamond button, aria-pressed); badge in list rows apps/web/src/routes/app.$workspaceId.$spaceId.$projectId.$listId.tsx:3126 and subtasks :2665; timeline apps/web/src/pages/workspace-timeline-page.tsx:447, 463, 526; strings catalogs.ts:1849-1853, 3383
rundesk_status.notes: Implemented as a separate boolean flag, NOT as a task type. That satisfies the spirit of her 03:13-03:31 point (a month-long deliverable is a Milestone, not a task) and is well surfaced — amber diamond on list rows, subtasks and the Gantt. But it is not settable at create time either (tasks.controller.ts:144 is on PATCH only) and it is orthogonal to the task_types vocabulary, so the two concepts can disagree.

rundesk_status.evidence: apps/api/src/modules/search/search.controller.ts:25-77 lists every accepted query param (types, statusCategory, priority, assigneeId, creatorId, includeArchived, labelId, dueAfter, dueBefore, customFieldId, customFieldValue, sort) — no taskTypeId; `SearchFilters` at apps/api/src/modules/search/search.service.ts:33-60 has no such key; palette filter panel apps/web/src/components/command-palette.tsx:402-556 has no such group
rundesk_status.notes: Note `types` in this API means ENTITY type (task/doc/file/user/comment/channel/message, search.service.ts:18), not ClickUp task type — easy to mistake for parity when grepping.

rundesk_status.evidence: apps/api/src/modules/search/search.controller.ts:25-43 has no spaceId/projectId/listId param; apps/api/src/modules/search/search.service.ts:313 builds `const filterExpr = [`workspaceId = "${workspaceId}"`]` and adds nothing else before passing it at :323
rundesk_status.notes: The index already declares `filterableAttributes: ['entityType', 'workspaceId', 'listId', 'spaceId']` (search.service.ts:122) and every indexed task/doc already carries listId and spaceId (:132-159), so the storage side is ready; only the param, the clause and the UI are absent.

rundesk_status.evidence: apps/web/src/components/command-palette.tsx:493-497 (FilterGroup 'Archived' with an 'Include archived' chip); catalogs.ts:4621-4622; apps/api/src/modules/search/search.controller.ts:36, :60; applied at apps/api/src/modules/search/search.service.ts:359 (tasks) and :417 (docs)

One divergence worth knowing: when includeArchived is on, search.service.ts:312 skips the Meili path entirely and falls back to Postgres ILIKE, because the index only holds non-archived rows (:207, :209, :226) — so result quality changes when the toggle flips.

rundesk_status.feature: Federated search across Google Drive / Gmail / SharePoint
rundesk_status.evidence: apps/api/src/modules/search/search.service.ts:18 fixes the universe to 'task'|'doc'|'file'|'user'|'comment'|'channel'|'message'; the 'file' branch queries only `taskAttachments` (:610-634) and R2 clip object keys (:644-675); no source-tab UI in apps/web/src/components/command-palette.tsx (searched for drive/gmail/sharepoint/source/tab)
rundesk_status.notes: No external source is ever queried at search time, and the palette has no source picker row, no per-source shortcut and no connect affordance.

rundesk_status.feature: Google Drive connection (OAuth, attach + preview on a task)
rundesk_status.evidence: apps/api/src/modules/integrations/connections/integration-connections.service.ts:84 ('google-drive' in listSupportedProviders), OAuth start/callback at :108-160, scopes at :464-467; provider card at apps/web/src/pages/workspace-integrations-page.tsx:48; link parsing apps/api/src/modules/tasks/external-links.util.ts + dto/external-link.dto.ts:3; Drive metadata fetch tasks.service.ts:962-963 and :1066 (GOOGLE_DRIVE_API_URL); inline preview apps/web/src/components/task-detail-sheet.tsx:1927-2003
rundesk_status.notes: Real, working OAuth with token refresh and health states — but scoped to `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` (line 467), i.e. only files the app created or the user explicitly picked. That scope cannot enumerate or search a user's Drive, so the connection as built is a prerequisite for, not a step toward, the federated search she describes.

gaps.title: Remove the language dropdown from the top bar and default the app to English
gaps.ask: "Yahan se English/Urdu — yeh cheez hata sakte hain; is ko hum logon ko yahan se REMOVE karna chahiye. Default par." — the language selector should not sit in the top bar; ship English by default.
gaps.why: The picker is rendered unconditionally at app-topbar.tsx:109 and is the second-most prominent control after "+ New". Removing it needs three things or a member loses the ability to change language at all: (a) drop it from the top bar, (b) add a Language row to Profile → General next to the existing theme selector (today language lives only in workspace Settings → General, an admin-labelled area, plus login/register/landing), (c) stop the browser-language auto-adopt in i18n.tsx:21-30 so a machine set to ur/ar no longer boots the UI in Urdu against the account default of 'en'. While in there, wire the dead FLAGS.UI_LANG_URDU / UI_LANG_ARABIC flags into the locale list so an admin can actually restrict the offered languages.

gaps.title: No way to configure the nav / top bar — add a nav customization setting
gaps.ask: "Lekin humare paas NAV BAR ko set down karne ka option nahi hai; lekin ClickUp pe humein option diya jaata hai." — ClickUp lets you configure what sits in the nav; Rundesk does not.
gaps.why: apps/web/src/components/app-topbar.tsx:89-114 is a fixed row (timer, search, AI, New, language, theme, bell, avatar) with no per-user or per-workspace setting to hide, reorder or pin items — which is precisely why the language dropdown cannot simply be switched off today. The dock has appearance settings (workspace-sidebar.tsx:1404-1490: orientation, opacity, size, reset) but its item list is hard-coded at :1376-1392, and the `pinnedLinks` jsonb column that exists for exactly this (packages/db/src/schema/user-dock-configs.ts:10, written by apps/api/src/modules/dashboards/dashboards.controller.ts:72-79) is read by nothing in the web app. Extend that stored config to cover top-bar items and dock items, and surface it as "Customize navigation" in Profile (per-user) with a workspace-level default for admins.

gaps.title: Notification bell duplicates the Inbox and offers members no way to configure notifications from it
gaps.ask: "Hum notification yahan le ke jaa rahe hain, to humein yahan bhi rakhne ki zaroorat nahi hai — just access; ya phir humein rakhne ki zaroorat hai to yeh option jo hai woh humare members ke paas hona chahiye, kyunke yahan se set down kar sakein." — notifications are moving into the Inbox, so the bell should either go or be pure quick-access with member-level settings reachable from it.
gaps.why: The bell popover (app-topbar.tsx:663-762) is a second, thinner copy of the Inbox: same list, same "Mark all read", and a "View all" footer — but no route to preferences, so a member who wants to turn something off from where they saw it has nowhere to click. The preference matrix itself already exists and is member-accessible (push-notifications-panel.tsx:17-50, mounted at app-profile-page.tsx:863), and the Inbox page already links to it (workspace-inbox-page.tsx:375-385). The fix is small: add a settings/gear row to the bell popover footer next to "View all" (and, if the bell is to be demoted to quick-access, make it hideable via the nav-customization work above).

gaps.title: AI chats are not saved — no conversation list, no "Ask, Build, Create"
gaps.ask: "Yeh AI CHATS hain… AI ka involvement bohot zyada hai — naya ClickUp ka vision mainly AI par depend karta hai." ClickUp keeps AI chats as durable objects in the sidebar with a "+ Ask, Build, Create" row and a Ctrl+O global opener.
gaps.why: Rundesk's assistant is stateless: ai-panel.tsx:61 holds the transcript in React state and replays it on each POST /api/v1/ai/chat (ai-panel.tsx:100-107); apps/api/src/modules/ai/ai.controller.ts:225 streams back without persisting; there is no chat/thread table anywhere in packages/db/src/schema (only ai-usage.ts). Closing the panel or reloading loses the conversation, so nothing can be resumed, shared, searched or listed. Needs a table (thread + messages, workspace + user scoped), CRUD endpoints, a sidebar "AI Chats" section with a new-chat row, and a keyboard shortcut — shortcuts-overlay.tsx:17-27 currently registers no AI shortcut at all.

gaps.title: No AI Agents product
gaps.ask: "AI — in ki CHATS hain, AI AGENTS hain, aur BRAIN hai. Unhon ne teen apne software launch kiye hain." ClickUp exposes an "Agents" control in every view header alongside Brain and Share.
gaps.why: Rundesk has deliberately shipped no agents — apps/web/src/lib/i18n/catalogs.ts:1251-1254 states it outright ("§A6.6 — there are no agents: the AI surface is an assistant"), and a repo-wide grep for 'agent' turns up only the bounded tool-use loop in apps/api/src/modules/ai/ai-command.ts and ai.service.ts:1875-2031, which is a one-shot preview-then-execute planner with no identity, no schedule and no attachment to a space or view. If we are matching ClickUp's three-product AI story, this is the whole third leg: named agents, scoped to a space/list/channel, with triggers and a per-view entry point.

gaps.title: Brain has no branded, always-present entry point
gaps.ask: ClickUp puts "✳ Brain²" in the view header of every surface, and names it in the AI Chats tooltip ("Open your AI Brain² Chats"), so the knowledge layer is one click from wherever you are.
gaps.why: The capability exists — retrieval with sources and reindex over workspace content (apps/api/src/modules/ai/knowledge.controller.ts, knowledge-indexer.service.ts, packages/db/src/schema/knowledge-embeddings.ts, UI at apps/web/src/pages/workspace-ai-page.tsx:184-345) — but it is buried as the second tab of /ai. gaps.ask: 'Yeh meri profile hai; yeh mujhe show karti hai ke meri activity kya hai, meri email kya hai, mera time zone kya chal raha hai, main kis ki team member hoon, meri priorities kya hain' — one panel that answers who this person is and what they are working on, opened over whatever page you are already on.
gaps.why: Rundesk's /app/profile (apps/web/src/pages/app-profile-page.tsx:29-33) is a General/Security/Notifications settings screen and it is a full-page navigation, so you lose your place. The only tabbed person panel is buried in the chat page (workspace-chat-page.tsx:3383), opens only by clicking a message author (:1799,:1814), and is `hidden xl:flex` (:3408) so it never renders under 1280px. There is no way to look up a colleague's profile from anywhere else in the app.

gaps.title: A person's local time is never shown
gaps.ask: 'Mera time zone kya chal raha hai' — the profile shows '5:28 pm local time' for the person you are looking at.
gaps.why: `users.timezone` is stored (packages/db/src/schema/users.ts:12) and used server-side for quiet hours (apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notifications.service.ts:1028-1055), and /app/profile lets you type it (app-profile-page.tsx:286-290) — but it is never rendered as a clock, for yourself or anyone else. Worse, `listMembers` does not select it (apps/api/src/modules/workspaces/workspaces.service.ts:566-579), so the roster payload cannot compute it. For a distributed team this is the single most-used fact on a profile.

gaps.title: Priorities — no 'today's most important tasks' list
gaps.ask: 'Meri priorities kya hain — yaani ke aaj ke din mein mere kaun se important task hain jo karne hain', with a '+ Add' and the empty state '+ Add your most important tasks here.'
gaps.why: Nothing in the codebase implements this: no 'Priorities'/'mostImportant'/'myPriorities' string in apps/web/src or catalogs.ts. The nearest thing is favorites (packages/db/src/schema/favorites.ts:19), which permanently pins a task into the sidebar rail — a bookmark, not a daily ordered shortlist. This is the one thing on the ClickUp profile that is a user-curated *decision* rather than a derived list, so nothing else substitutes for it.

gaps.title: Tasks buckets: Next, Unscheduled, Done and Delegated are missing; Today and Overdue are merged
gaps.ask: 'Yahan bhi bata raha hai ke TODAY ke kya task hain, OVERDUE kaun se ho gaye the, NEXT kaun se upcoming task mere paas aa sakte hain, kaun si aisi cheezein jo maine CREATE ki hain par abhi tak maine kisi ko assign nahi kiya' — six counted, collapsible buckets, with a '+' quick-add on Next.
gaps.why: Rundesk Home offers only 'Assigned to me' and a single combined 'Today & Overdue' item (apps/web/src/routes/app.$workspaceId.tsx:262-266, rendered :339-359). Today and Overdue need to be separate rows with independent counts; 'Next' (upcoming), 'Unscheduled' (created but never scheduled/assigned), 'Done' and 'Delegated' have no equivalent anywhere. The chat panel's Tasks tab (workspace-chat-page.tsx:3483-3503) is one flat list of 6 with no buckets or counts. 'Unscheduled' in particular is the accountability view — what you created and then dropped.

gaps.title: Org chart is admin-only, hidden by default, and not on a person
gaps.ask: 'Yahan mujhe ORGANIZATION CHART show ho jayega' — the person's reporting line drawn as manager node → arrow → their card, with a 'No manager' placeholder when unset, plus 'Explore the full org chart / 1 person in your reporting line'.
gaps.why: The data and the admin editor are built (packages/db/src/schema/workspaces.ts:100; apps/api/src/modules/workspaces/workspaces.controller.ts:213-227 with cycle rejection at workspaces.service.ts:652-673), and `ReportingTree` exists — but at apps/web/src/pages/workspace-settings-page.tsx:1173-1224 it is (a) inside Workspace Settings → Members, (b) an indented text list with '└' glyphs rather than a diagram, and critically (c) `if (!members.some((m) => m.managerId)) return null` at :1175 — it renders nothing until an admin has filled in a manager, so most workspaces never see it exists. Do not rebuild the backend; surface it on the profile, add the 'No manager' root node, and add the 'Explore' escape to a full-workspace chart.

gaps.title: No calendar on a person, and Google Calendar sync is not discoverable from the profile
gaps.ask: 'CALENDAR — mera hi calendar show ho sakta hai, Google Calendar sync up kar sakti hoon.'
gaps.why: The sync engine is genuinely built (apps/api/src/modules/calendar-sync/calendar-sync.service.ts:19 — bidirectional Google + Outlook; wizard at apps/web/src/components/calendar-sync-wizard.tsx:30, mounted only at apps/web/src/pages/workspace-integrations-page.tsx:382). What is missing is the surface: the only calendar *views* are per-list (app.$workspaceId.$spaceId.$projectId.$listId.tsx:994), so there is no 'my calendar' across lists and no per-person calendar. The chat DM 'Calendar' tab (workspace-chat-page.tsx:1306) lists shared meetings, not a calendar. This is a view + a link, not new sync work.

gaps.title: No per-person task activity feed (and no search/filter on activity)
gaps.ask: 'Jis jis task ko open kiya hoga, jis document pe kaam kiya hoga — bas woh yahan pe show honge', with a search icon and a filter icon on the feed header.
gaps.why: Activity is queryable by task (apps/api/src/modules/tasks/activity.controller.ts:11-20), by project (:24-40) and workspace-wide (apps/api/src/modules/reports/reports.controller.ts:184-192) — but never by actor. The only per-member activity endpoint is chat messages (apps/api/src/modules/chat/chat.controller.ts:149), and its own empty state admits the limitation: catalogs.ts:3137 'No recent activity in loaded messages.' `task_activity.actorId` already exists (packages/db/src/schema/activity.ts:11), so this is mostly a new filtered query plus the search/filter controls.

gaps.title: 'Add time off' is not reachable from a profile
gaps.ask: '+ Add time off' sits as the first row of the profile's Activity tab, right above the person's contact details.
gaps.why: Time off is fully built (apps/api/src/modules/time-off/, schema packages/db/src/schema/time-off.ts) but its only UI is a collapsed accordion titled 'Time away' inside the Workload page (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-workload-page.tsx:355-381, strings catalogs.ts:4987-4994). Nobody books leave by first navigating to a capacity heat map. Reuse the existing endpoints from the profile panel.

gaps.title: 'Set status' — no custom status message, only four fixed presence values
gaps.ask: A 'Set status' row in the avatar menu, separate from online/offline, plus the status pill on the profile header ('⊘ Offline').
gaps.why: packages/db/src/schema/users.ts:53 constrains `presenceStatus` to 'online' | 'away' | 'busy' | 'offline', and the picker (apps/web/src/components/app-topbar.tsx:769-774) offers Auto / Away / Do not disturb / Invisible. There is no free-text or emoji status the workspace can read ('on site till 4', 'in a workshop'). Separately, the chat profile panel's status is broken: workspace-chat-page.tsx:3431-3432 hard-codes a green dot and `t('chat.online')` for every member regardless of their actual presenceStatus — it will tell you someone is Online when they are Invisible.

gaps.title: Team membership is not visible or selectable from a person's profile
gaps.ask: 'Main kis ki TEAM MEMBER hoon — yahan pe main woh select down kar sakti hoon.'
gaps.why: Teams exist as workspace Groups with per-member resolution already in the roster payload (apps/api/src/modules/workspaces/workspaces.service.ts:606-616,630) and chips rendered at apps/web/src/pages/workspace-settings-page.tsx:1080-1091 — but only inside the admin Members tab, labelled 'Groups' (catalogs.ts:4591) rather than 'Teams' (the string catalogs.ts:3211 'nav.teams' already exists). A regular member cannot see which teams they are in from their own profile. Data is done; this is surfacing plus a naming decision.

gaps.title: No 'Get StandUp' — no per-person work summary
gaps.ask: A '✦ Get StandUp' button sitting next to the message button in the profile header, generating what this person has been doing.
gaps.why: Zero implementation: grepping 'standup|stand.?up' across apps/ returns only two unrelated test fixtures (apps/api/src/modules/tasks/external-links.test.ts:449, apps/api/src/modules/chat/chat.service.test.ts:128). Rundesk does have the ingredients — a daily AI briefing (apps/web/src/pages/app-profile-page.tsx:876-963, `briefing` prefs) and per-member contribution analytics (apps/api/src/modules/reports/reports.controller.ts:199-214) — but neither is an on-demand 'what has this person been up to' summary you can pull from their profile.

gaps.title: Avatar menu is thin: no Notifications, Themes, Keyboard shortcuts, or Personal Tools section
gaps.ask: The dropdown behind the avatar carries Set status, Mute notifications, Settings, Notifications, Themes, Keyboard shortcuts, Download app, Help, then a 'Personal Tools' block: Create task, My Work, Track Time, Notepad, Record a Clip, Talk to Text, Create Reminder, Create Doc, Create Whiteboard, View People, Create Dashboard.
gaps.why: apps/web/src/components/app-topbar.tsx:846-916 has only presence, mute, Profile, Workspace settings, Help & support, Reset dock, Sign out. Several targets already exist and just are not linked from here — the shortcuts overlay is mounted at routes/app.tsx:141 (component shortcuts-overlay.tsx:62), theme strings at catalogs.ts:3266-3270, Track Time / Clips / Whiteboards / Dashboards are all routes. Genuinely absent as features: Notepad (no hits anywhere in apps/web/src), Talk to Text, a standalone Create Reminder (reminders are task-scoped only — apps/web/src/components/task-reminders.tsx, catalogs.ts:2082-2092), and 'View People' (there is no workspace people directory; admin-directory-page.tsx is a super-admin cross-workspace user list). Treat the menu wiring as small and the four missing tools as separate items.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Clicking the avatar in the far-right of the top bar opens a single scrollable dropdown that is both the identity surface and the personal-tools launcher. It shows who you are and your live availability, offers the two 'am I reachable' controls at the top (Set status, Mute notifications), then a block of app-level personal entries, then a pinnable Personal Tools block.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Order, top to bottom: (1) header row = avatar with green presence dot + display name 'Hamda Tahir' + second line showing the resolved presence word 'Online'; (2) 'Set status' (smiley icon); (3) 'Mute notifications' (speaker-off icon) with a right chevron '>' indicating a submenu; (4) divider; (5) 'Settings' (gear); (6) 'Notifications' (bell); (7) 'Themes' (paint icon); (8) 'Keyboard shortcuts' (⌘ icon); (9) 'Download ClickUp' (grid icon, external-link glyph on the right edge); (10) 'Help' (? icon, glyph on the right); (11) section label 'Personal Tools' in small caps; (12) Create task, My Work, Track Time, Notepad, Record a Clip, Talk to Text, Create Reminder, Create Doc, Create Whiteboard, View People, Create Dashboard — most rows carry a pin icon on the right to pin them to the top bar. The menu scrolls internally.

clickup_spec.behaviour: A modal that lets a person publish what they are doing right now plus how long it lasts, so teammates who missed the group message still know. Distinct from automatic presence: it is free text + emoji + an availability/duration, and it expires by itself.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Modal titled 'Set status' with a close X. Row 1: a circular emoji-picker button (default smiley) then a text input with placeholder "What's on your mind?". Below, section 'Recents' listing previously-used statuses: 🍎 'Namaz Break — OOO for 30 minutes', 'Break — for an hour', 'Focusing — for 4 hours', then a 'Show more' link. Each preset renders as '<emoji> <bold label> — <availability/duration>' where availability is either implicit-available ('for an hour') or 'OOO …'. Footer: 'Cancel' and a primary 'Save' button with a ⏎ hint, disabled until there is text. The list scrolls.

clickup_spec.feature: Personal Tools section in the avatar menu
clickup_spec.behaviour: Clicking the avatar in the top-right opens a dropdown. Below the account rows (Set status, Mute notifications, Settings, Notifications, Themes, Keyboard shortcuts, Download ClickUp, Help) there is a labelled section "Personal Tools" that acts as a launcher for the account-level quick actions. The list is scrollable inside the dropdown.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Section label "Personal Tools" rendered as small muted text, no divider above it beyond the existing one after Help. Rows in this exact order: Create task, My Work, Track Time, Notepad, Record a Clip, Talk to Text, Create Reminder, Create Doc, Create Whiteboard, View People, Create Dashboard. Each row = leading 16px outline icon + label, left-aligned. Icons observed: circle-check-plus, briefcase, stopwatch, clipboard, video-camera, microphone, alarm-clock, document, whiteboard, two-people, bar-chart. Dropdown is ~320px wide, anchored under the avatar, with its own vertical scrollbar and a down-chevron affordance at the bottom edge when more rows exist below the fold.

clickup_spec.feature: Pin / unpin a tool to the top bar
clickup_spec.behaviour: Every Personal Tools row carries a pushpin toggle on its right edge. Toggling the pin adds or removes that tool's icon from the persistent icon strip in the app top bar, immediately, without closing the menu or reloading. Pin state is per-user and persists.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Pin icon sits flush against the right edge of the row. Two visual states are distinguishable: dark/filled pin = pinned (Track Time, Notepad, Record a Clip, Talk to Text, Create Doc, Create Dashboard, and Create task drawn lighter), and no pin rendered at rest for rows that are not pinned (My Work, Create Reminder, Create Whiteboard, View People) — i.e. the pin affordance for an unpinned row only appears on hover. Not every tool is pinnable-by-default; the set is user-chosen, not fixed.

clickup_spec.feature: Pinned-tool icon strip in the top bar
clickup_spec.behaviour: The pinned tools render as a horizontal row of icon-only buttons in the top bar, immediately to the left of the user avatar and to the right of the global search field and the AI Chats pill. Clicking an icon launches that tool directly. The strip re-flows when items are unpinned — remaining icons shift right toward the avatar and the group divider disappears when the strip empties down.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Before unpinning (07:48 / 08:03): 7 icons — Create task, Track Time, Notepad, Record a Clip, Talk to Text, Create Doc, Create Dashboard — then a thin vertical divider, then the avatar with a chevron. After unpinning (08:26): 3 icons — Create task, Record a Clip, Create Dashboard — divider gone, icons sit adjacent to the avatar. Icons are ~20px monochrome outline, evenly spaced (~24px pitch), no labels, no badges. Whole strip is right-aligned in the 32px-tall top bar.

clickup_spec.feature: Tool catalog behind the Personal Tools list
clickup_spec.behaviour: The eleven Personal Tools are the account-level things a person creates or opens without first navigating into a Space/List: create a task anywhere, open My Work, start a time tracker, open a Notepad, record a screen/webcam clip, dictate via Talk to Text, create a standalone reminder, create a Doc, create a Whiteboard, view People, create a Dashboard.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Ordering is fixed and is NOT alphabetical or grouped — creation actions, personal views and viewers are interleaved: Create task, My Work, Track Time, Notepad, Record a Clip, Talk to Text, Create Reminder, Create Doc, Create Whiteboard, View People, Create Dashboard.

gaps.title: Per-user pinnable tools in the top bar (pin/unpin from a Personal Tools menu)
gaps.ask: Users should decide which tools sit in the top bar for easy access and which do not — instead of us shipping a fixed limited set they have to live with. She unpins Track Time / Notepad / Talk to Text / Create Doc in ClickUp, the icons vanish from the top bar, and she says this is the model we should give too.
gaps.why: apps/web/src/components/app-topbar.tsx:102-113 hardcodes the header contents (TimerIndicator, SearchBar, AiDockToggle, QuickCreateButton, LanguageSwitcher, ThemeToggle, NotificationsBell, UserMenu) — nothing is configurable. The floating dock at apps/web/src/components/workspace-sidebar.tsx:1376-1392 is likewise a hardcoded DockLink list, and its settings panel (lines 1404-1486) exposes only orientation, opacity, size and reset-position. The storage already exists and is unused: packages/db/src/schema/user-dock-configs.ts:10 defines `pinned_links` jsonb, apps/api/src/modules/dashboards/dashboards.service.ts:269-295 already persists a `pinnedLinks` patch, and apps/api/src/modules/dashboards/dashboards.controller.ts:66-79 already exposes GET/POST — but a repo-wide grep for `pinnedLinks` finds no web caller. So this is: define a tool registry, render the pinned subset in the top bar, and add pin toggles in the user menu, all against an endpoint that already works.

gaps.title: "Personal Tools" launcher section in the user/avatar menu
gaps.ask: When you click your profile there should be a TOOLS list — task creation, timing, notepad, clip recording, voice, doc, whiteboard, dashboard — each with a pin toggle.
gaps.why: Our avatar dropdown (apps/web/src/components/app-topbar.tsx:836-919) only carries identity, presence, mute, Profile, Workspace settings, Help & support, Reset dock and Sign out. There is no launcher list, so there is nowhere for the pin affordance from the item above to live, and there is no single place a user can see everything they can create. Needs a catalog entry per tool (icon + label + action or route + feature-flag/permission gate) reused by both the menu and the top-bar strip.

gaps.title: Notepad — personal scratch notes

Docs are workspace/space-scoped content; a Notepad is a private, always-available jot surface with its own table (user-scoped, not workspace content) and a popover editor. Without it, the pinned-tools strip will have a hole where ClickUp has an icon.

gaps.title: Standalone reminder not bound to a task

A user cannot set "remind me at 4pm" without first inventing a task. Fix is making taskId nullable plus a create-reminder entry point; the notification delivery pipeline already exists.

Dictation (apps/web/src/lib/use-speech-recognition.ts) is only mounted in the AI composer — apps/web/src/components/ai-panel.tsx:312 and apps/web/src/pages/workspace-ai-page.tsx:493. The header timer (apps/web/src/components/app-topbar.tsx:287-366) returns null with no active timer and can only stop one; starting happens in task-detail-sheet.tsx:4174 or workspace-time-page.tsx:203-205. gaps.title: Sidebar nav Favorites are browser-local, not account-level
gaps.ask: The whole point of pinning your tools is that YOUR choice follows you. ClickUp's pin state is on the account.
gaps.why: Our nearest existing customisation writes to localStorage only — apps/web/src/components/workspace-sidebar.tsx:519-541 reads `rundesk.navFavorites.{workspaceId}` and lines 551-566 write it; nothing hits the API. clickup_spec.behaviour: Clicking the workspace pill in the top-left opens a dropdown panel. Header block: workspace avatar (colored square with first letter), workspace name, and a metadata line. In frame 134 the line reads "2 members • Free Forever"; in frames 146/149 (the brand-new workspace) it reads "Free Forever • Upgrade", where Upgrade is a link. Immediately below the header sit two equal-width buttons side by side. In the Leo workspace they are [gear] Settings and [person+] Invite; in the new xyzzzjnjsnjd workspace they are [gear] Settings and [people] People. Below that a section labelled "Manage" lists five rows with icons: Apps, Templates, Custom Fields, Automations, Tag Manager (with a purple "New" pill). Below that a section labelled "Switch Workspaces" — in the new-workspace frames it also carries a magnifier/search icon on the right of the section header — listing every workspace the user belongs to, each as an avatar square + name: The AURA AGENCY (red unread dot on the avatar), BB - Team, Nikki Lowe, Ai Agents testing, Hamda Tahir's Workspace, Leo. The list scrolls with its own scrollbar. Pinned at the bottom of the panel, full width, is a bordered button "+ Create Workspace".
clickup_spec.ui_details: Order top→bottom: avatar+name+plan line; [Settings][Invite|People] row; "Manage" heading (10px uppercase muted) → Apps / Templates / Custom Fields / Automations / Tag Manager [New]; "Switch Workspaces" heading (+ search icon) → scrollable workspace rows with letter-avatars; footer "+ Create Workspace" button. Current workspace is NOT shown in the Switch list header area — it is the header itself. Unread activity in another workspace is a small red dot on that workspace's avatar.

clickup_spec.behaviour: "+ Create Workspace" navigates to app.clickup.com/team-setup/additional and opens a full-screen onboarding modal — the same wizard shape used at signup, minus the account step. The modal is centered, has the ClickUp logo top-left and a close ✕ top-right, a large heading, the step's controls, a thin horizontal progress bar near the bottom, and Back / Next buttons on the last steps. The wizard advances through: (1) purpose, (2) tool search / skip, (3) feature picker, (4) workspace name, then Finish.
clickup_spec.ui_details: URL app.clickup.com/team-setup/additional, tab title "Onboarding | ClickUp". Progress bar sits ~40px above the modal bottom edge and fills left→right (≈8% on the purpose step, ≈75% on the feature step). Back button is "‹ Back" ghost style bottom-left; Next is "Next ›" dark filled bottom-right. ✕ closes and abandons creation.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Step 1 of the create-workspace wizard asks "What will you use this Workspace for?" with three mutually-exclusive pill buttons in a row: Work, Personal, School. A footnote with an ⓘ icon sits under the progress bar: "Keep in mind info can't be transferred across Workspaces."
clickup_spec.ui_details: Heading is large serif-ish display text, left-aligned. Buttons are wide rounded-rect outlines, roughly 140px each, evenly spaced, left-aligned under the heading. Footnote text is small and muted with a circled-i glyph.

clickup_spec.behaviour: A later step lets the user skip and/or search for a different tool they currently use (so ClickUp can offer an import path). The consultant says at 08:54 "Skip [ya] step, aur yahan se different tool search kar sakti hoon" — the step is skippable and carries a tool search box.
clickup_spec.feature: Wizard step — Skip / search another tool

clickup_spec.behaviour: Step asks "Which features are you interested in trying?" and shows an 18-tile multi-select grid, 4 tiles per row. Each tile is a rounded rect with a leading monochrome icon, the feature name, and a circular checkbox on the right that fills with a dark check when selected. Tiles read, in order: Boards & Kanban, Docs & Wikis, Automations, CRM / Whiteboards, Chat, Dashboards, Clips / Tasks & Projects, Time Tracking, Goals & OKRs, Forms / Scheduling, AI, Workload, Sprints / Gantt Charts, Calendar. In the captured state Automations, CRM, Chat, Dashboards, Clips, Goals & OKRs, Forms and Sprints are checked; the rest are unchecked. Progress bar is ~75% filled. Footer shows "‹ Back" and "Next ›".

Checkbox is a 16px circle on the tile's right edge; unchecked = hollow ring, checked = filled dark circle with white tick. Last row is short (2 tiles) and left-aligned, not stretched.

clickup_spec.behaviour: The wizard asks for the workspace name ("xyz likhoongi to meri new workspace ka naam hai") and the final button is Finish, which creates the workspace. A full-page loading screen (white, centered animated logo mark) then runs while the workspace is provisioned, and the app lands directly inside the new workspace.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Transcript 09:02–09:07. After Finish, tab title stays "Onboarding | ClickUp" during the white loading screen, then the URL becomes app.clickup.com/<newWorkspaceId>/v/o/s/<spaceId> and the tab becomes "List | List | xyzzzjnjsnjd (Overview)".

clickup_spec.behaviour: A freshly created workspace is NOT empty. It arrives pre-seeded with: a Space named "Space" containing a List named "List"; an "All Tasks - <workspace>" pseudo-space; two chat channels, "General - <workspace>" and "Welcome"; a Direct Messages entry for the creator; an "AI Chats / Ask, Build, Create" entry; and the standard left nav (Home, Inbox, Replies, Skills, Meetings, My Tasks, More). The list view opens on a "TO DO 0" group with columns Name, Assignee, Due date, Priority and an "Add Task" placeholder row.

List toolbar: Group: Status | Subtasks | Columns, and on the right Filter, Closed, Assignee, avatar, search, Customize, [Add Task ▾]. Space header: breadcrumb "S Space / ≔ List" + star, tabs "Add Channel | List | Board | + View", right-side eye/watch, Agents, ⚡, Brain², Share.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Creating a workspace is a right every ordinary member holds, not an admin-only action — "WORKSPACE IS A FEATURE jo ke har member kar sakta hai; it's not necessary ke humare paas kuch admin hi aaye jo kar sake". The permission must be gated DOWN, not up: member = can create, admin = can create, GUEST = cannot create, VIEWER = cannot create, everyone else = can create.
clickup_spec.feature: Who may create a workspace (permission model)
clickup_spec.ui_details: Transcript 09:13–09:39. Implication: the "+ Create Workspace" entry must be hidden/disabled for guest and viewer roles and visible for member/manager/admin.

clickup_spec.behaviour: A workspace a user creates belongs to that user's email, and sharing it with teammates is the creator's own decision — nothing is auto-shared, and content cannot move between workspaces ("Keep in mind info can't be transferred across Workspaces"). Switching between workspaces reloads the whole app (full skeleton + logo spinner) because the two workspaces share no data.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Transcript 09:43–09:48. Frame 150 shows the full-app loading skeleton on workspace switch: grey placeholder bars top and bottom, centered ClickUp logo, tab title already switched to "All Tasks | Leo (List)".

clickup_spec.behaviour: The account-level settings page (app.clickup.com/<id>/settings/profile) carries a "My Settings" section in its left nav whose entries are Preferences, Notifications, Workspaces, Chat, Referrals — i.e. a dedicated per-user page listing every workspace the account belongs to, separate from any single workspace's settings.

gaps.title: Workspace creation is super-admin-only; must be opened to member/manager/admin and closed to guest (and viewer)
gaps.why: apps/api/src/modules/workspaces/workspaces.controller.ts:35-44 hard-rejects every caller whose global role is not 'super_admin' with ForbiddenException('Only a Super Admin can create additional workspaces'). There is no 'workspace.create' key anywhere in the permission catalog (apps/api/src/modules/custom-roles/permission-catalog.ts:10-43 lists only workspace.manage / billing / delete / audit.view), so custom roles cannot grant it either. Meanwhile the web UI offers the action to EVERYONE: the "New workspace" button in the switcher (apps/web/src/components/workspace-sidebar.tsx:726-737) is inside the `openSwitcher` block with no role guard at all, and submitWorkspaceDialog (same file:369-396) POSTs /workspaces then shows window.alert with the 403 text. So today a normal member sees the button, clicks it, and gets an error dialog. Also note Rundesk has no 'viewer' role at all — userRoleEnum in packages/db/src/schema/enums.ts:3-9 is super_admin | workspace_admin | manager | member | guest, and use-workspace-role.ts exposes isAdmin / isManagerOrAbove but no isGuest, so there is nothing to gate the button on.

gaps.ask: "Main 'New Workspace' par click karoongi, main new workspace bana sakti hoon — phir same layout jo aap ne abhi kiya tha [signup ke waqt]." … "To workspace jo new create hogi, us ka option bilkul same wohi hai jaise hum ClickUp mein login karte hain aur apni workspace create karte hain. To YEH FEATURE BHI MISSING HAI aap ke end par."
gaps.title: No in-app create-workspace wizard — 'New workspace' is a bare one-field name dialog
gaps.why: The multi-step wizard she is pointing at DOES exist in Rundesk, but only at signup: apps/web/src/pages/sign-up-page.tsx:61-225 renders StepAccount → StepWorkspace → StepFeatures → StepInvites → StepDone with a 'Step {n} of 4' label, a Progress bar, Back / Continue, and a 'Skip for now' button — and it is hard-wired to POST /auth/signup (finish() at sign-up-page.tsx:84-121), so it can only run for a logged-out visitor creating their FIRST workspace. The in-app path is completely different: the switcher's New-workspace action opens a generic ContainerEditDialog (workspace-sidebar.tsx:1535-1543) which, with no `fields` prop, renders a single 'Name' Input (apps/web/src/components/container-edit-dialog.tsx:100, 111-118). The /app index route offers the same thing — one Name field plus a Create button (apps/web/src/routes/app.index.tsx:127-156) — and is usually unreachable anyway because app.index.tsx:42-54 auto-redirects a user with exactly one workspace straight into it and sends super_admins to /app/admin. Work: extract the signup wizard's steps into a reusable component and mount it behind the switcher's New-workspace button, POSTing to /workspaces instead of /auth/signup.

gaps.ask: "Phir poochega — 'xyz' likhoongi to meri new workspace ka naam hai" preceded by the purpose question "What will you use this Workspace for? Work / Personal / School" seen on screen.

The nearest thing is the signup wizard's StepWorkspace, which asks for industry (Software / Marketing / Design / Operations / Other) and team size (Just me / 2–10 / 11–50 / 51–200 / 200+) — see the signUp.industry* and signUp.team* keys in apps/web/src/lib/i18n/catalogs.ts:1229-1240 — not Work/Personal/School. The workspaces table (packages/db/src/schema/workspaces.ts) has no column to store a purpose.

gaps.ask: Implicit in "same layout jo aap ne abhi kiya tha" — the feature picker she demonstrates (Automations, CRM, Chat, Dashboards, Clips, Goals & OKRs, Forms, Sprints checked) is supposed to actually configure the new workspace.
gaps.title: Feature-picker answers are collected and then silently thrown away
gaps.why: The web wizard sends features, industry and teamSize in the /auth/signup body (apps/web/src/pages/sign-up-page.tsx:95-104) and the DTO declares all three (apps/api/src/modules/auth/dto/signup.dto.ts:54, 59, 65), but grepping apps/api/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts for 'features', 'industry' and 'teamSize' returns nothing — signUp() (auth.service.ts:274-364) creates user → organization → organizationMembers → workspace → workspaceMembers → invitations and never reads them. gaps.title: A workspace a member creates is not private to them — it is attached to the caller's existing organization
gaps.why: WorkspacesService.create (apps/api/src/modules/workspaces/workspaces.service.ts:871-896) deliberately does NOT spin up a fresh org: it looks up the caller's oldest organizationMembers row and reuses that organizationId, only creating an org when the caller has none. Combined with GET /organizations/:organizationId/workspaces (apps/api/src/modules/organizations/organizations.controller.ts:66-71, guarded only by OrganizationAdminGuard), any org admin can enumerate the personal workspace a member just made. That contradicts 'woh meri email pe ban rahi hai' and the isolation promise on the ClickUp modal. Decide the intended model and either spawn a new org per user-created workspace or scope the org-admin listing.

clickup_spec.behaviour: ClickUp's left chrome is two independent columns. Column 1 is a permanent icon RAIL (icon + small text label under each icon) that never goes away. Column 2 is a wider contextual PANEL whose contents depend on the rail item selected (rail "Home" → panel listing Inbox/Replies/Skills/…, AI Chats, Channels, Direct Messages, Spaces). Only column 2 collapses; column 1 stays put so every top-level destination remains one click away at all times.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Rail entries top-to-bottom, each icon with its label rendered beneath it: Home, Spaces, Planner, AI, Teams, Docs, Dashboards, Forms, Clips, Goals, More, Invite. Active entry (Home) is drawn with a filled/branded icon. Rail is ~70px wide; panel is ~250px wide.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Hovering anywhere on the inner sidebar reveals a control cluster in its header. Clicking the "«" double-chevron collapses the whole inner panel to zero width; the main content immediately reflows to fill the reclaimed space. The control is hidden until hover so it costs no visual weight at rest.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Header row when hovered, left→right: title "Home", then a panel/inbox icon, a magnifier (search), a funnel (filter), then the "«" collapse chevron, then the black "+ Create" button flush right. At rest only "Home" and "+ Create" are visible. The cluster sits between the title and the Create button, not at the panel's outer edge.

clickup_spec.behaviour: With the panel closed the user still has full navigation: the icon rail persists with all twelve destinations and their labels. A "»" double-chevron appears at the very top of the rail (above a thin divider) as the re-open affordance. Re-opening restores the panel to exactly the same scroll position and contents it had before collapsing.
clickup_spec.ui_details: "»" chevron pinned to the top of the rail, above the Home icon, separated by a hairline divider. Rail items keep their labels while collapsed — the labels are part of the rail, not the panel. Content region grows by the panel's full width and its cards re-flow (the Recent/Docs/Bookmarks row visibly widens).
