clickup_spec.feature: Inbox tab strip (All / Primary / Other / Later / Cleared)
clickup_spec.behaviour: The Inbox is a full page reached from the Home sidebar item 'Inbox'. It is partitioned by five top-level tabs. 'All' shows every notification from everywhere the user is a member — group chatter, comments, anything. 'Primary' shows only the notification types the user has marked Important in Customize importance. 'Other' shows the rest (per the consultant it duplicates 'All' in practice). 'Later' holds snoozed/saved items. 'Cleared' holds dismissed items. The active tab is persisted in the URL as ?tab=<all|primary|other|later|cleared> so it survives navigation and is linkable.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Full-width horizontal tab strip pinned under the app topbar, five evenly spaced cells separated by hairline vertical dividers. Order and icons, left to right: 'All' (4-square grid icon), 'Primary' (tray/inbox icon), 'Other' (pulse/activity squiggle), 'Later' (clock), 'Cleared' (check-with-down-arrow). Active tab is marked by a thick bottom underline bar spanning the tab cell (not a pill). Hovering a tab paints a light background block over the whole cell. No counts shown next to the tab labels.

clickup_spec.behaviour: A thin toolbar sits directly beneath the tab strip and applies to whichever tab is open: a Filter entry point on the left, and on the right a gear that opens the Customize Inbox drawer plus a bulk 'Clear all' that empties the current tab.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Left: 'Filter' button with a funnel icon, small, borderless. Right, in order: gear icon (opens 'Customize Inbox'), then 'Clear all' with a double-check/down-arrow icon. Both right-hand controls are muted grey until hover.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Clicking the gear opens a right-hand drawer that controls how the inbox itself is presented — whether the All tab exists at all, whether rows are grouped into date buckets, sort direction, and whether opening a notification takes over the screen or expands in place. It also links out to the deeper importance settings, the account notification settings, and the shortcut reference.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Drawer header 'Customize Inbox' + X close. Three toggle rows, all default ON: 'Show All tab' (eye icon), 'Group by date' (stack/layers icon), 'Sort by newest first' (sort-descending icon). Section label 'Important notifications' then a navigation row 'Customize importance' (sliders icon) with the count of enabled-of-total on the right ('11/42') and a '>' chevron. Section label 'Display mode' with two picture-radio cards side by side: left = wide single-column wireframe, caption 'Fullscreen', radio unchecked; right = list-of-rows wireframe, caption 'Inline', blue filled check — Inline is selected. Footer links: 'Notification settings' (gear icon), 'Keyboard shortcuts' (command icon).

clickup_spec.behaviour: A sub-panel (opened from the drawer, with a back arrow to the parent) that decides which notification types are Important. Anything Important lands in Primary; everything else lands in Other. Toggling a row flips it and MOVES it live between the two sections — turn Reactions off and it drops out of 'Important' and reappears under 'Not Important'. Changes are forward-only: they do not reclassify notifications already received.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Header: '<' back arrow + 'Customize importance' + X close. Search field with magnifier and placeholder 'Search...'. Section 'Important' (rows in this order, all toggled ON): Mentioning me (@), New comments (speech bubble), Assigned to me (person), Assigned to my Team (people), Added to my priorities (person+arrow) — these five render dimmed with pale toggles, i.e. locked on — then Reactions (thumbs-up), Shared with me (share), Access requests (hands), Assigned comments (person), Assignee change (two people), Follower change (bell). Helper line under the list: 'Any changes to these settings will only take effect on new notifications.' Section 'Not Important' (toggled OFF): Resolved comments (check), Task created (check-circle), Subtask created (branch), Status change (circle) — the list scrolls, total is 42 types per the '11/42' counter on the parent row. Sticky footer link: 'Reset to default'. Rows highlight on hover; the toggle is the whole control.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Empty tabs get a purpose-built celebratory/onboarding state rather than a generic blank.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Zero-notification state: tray illustration with a green check badge, surrounded by floating rounded-square tiles (# channel, doc, comment bubble, marker) joined by dotted swirls; caption "You've achieved Inbox Zero!". Zero-collaborator state: heading 'Looking to collaborate?', sub-line 'Collaboration is one invite away.', dark pill CTA 'Invite people'.

clickup_spec.behaviour: A bell icon on the task adds followers. A follower who is NOT an assignee still receives every notification for that task. This is the mechanism behind the 'Follower change' notification type in Customize importance.
clickup_spec.ui_details: In the quick-create Task modal the bell sits in the footer control row between the paperclip (attachment) icon and the 'Create Task' split button. Modal chrome: header 'Task' with tab-style underline, minimize arrow, X; pills 'Select List... ˅' and 'Task ˅'; title input placeholder "Task Name or type '/' for commands"; description placeholder 'Add description, or write with ✨ AI'; 'Assignee' button and '…' overflow; footer 'Templates' on the left, paperclip + bell + 'Create Task ˅' on the right.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Inbox is the first item under Home in the second sidebar column; clicking it navigates to /inbox?tab=all.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Sidebar column header 'Home' with search, filter and '«' collapse icons plus a '+ Create' button. Items in order: Inbox, Replies, Skills, Meetings, My Tasks, '… More'. Then sections 'AI Chats' (New Conversation ×3, '… More'), 'Channels' (# Welcome, General - Leo, + Add Channel), 'Direct Messages' (Hamda Tahir — You, suleman, + New message).

gaps.title: Customize importance: user-controlled Important / Not Important per notification type
gaps.ask: 'Primary pe yeh setting ka option hai... yeh mujh se poochta hai ke mujhe kya cheezein show karwani hain. Phir yahan pe CUSTOMIZE hai: mention... comment... assign... priorities... Reactions mujhe na show hon, shared with me na show ho... Yeh log ne neeche saare ke saare inhein long list likh ke rakhi hai; aap chaho to show kar sakte hain. Phir aap ko Primary mein sirf wohi notifications show honge jo aap chahte hain.'
gaps.why: Today Primary/Other is a hardcoded set in the frontend (workspace-inbox-page.tsx:176-183) — the user cannot change what lands in Primary at all. This is the single feature the whole Inbox segment of the walkthrough is about: an inbox you can only read is useless at 200 notifications; the point is deciding which twenty matter. Needs a persisted per-type importance map (extend the notification_preferences JSONB), an API to read/write it, and the panel UI: search box, 'Important' section, 'Not Important' section, toggling a row moves it live between sections, helper line 'Any changes to these settings will only take effect on new notifications.', and a 'Reset to default' footer. Move matchesInboxFilter off the constant and onto the stored map.

gaps.title: Drop the 'Other' chip from the inbox
gaps.ask: 'Ab yahan jo OTHERS wala option hai — yeh mujhe NAHI CHAHIYE humari list mein, kyunke yahan bhi same All wale hi hain — to yeh nahi chahiye. Lekin LATER ka chahiye.'
gaps.why: She looked at ClickUp's Other tab, judged it a duplicate of All, and ruled it out for Rundesk. We currently ship it: the chip is rendered at workspace-inbox-page.tsx:414 from the ('all','primary','other') tuple, labelled 'inbox.filterOther' (catalogs.ts:4641) with hint 'inbox.filterOtherHint' (:4644), and 'other' is an accepted URL value in app.$workspaceId.inbox.tsx:4. Remove the chip and the filter value, keep the predicate (Primary still needs 'is this human traffic'), and redirect any bookmarked ?filter=other to 'all' the same way ?filter=mentions is already remapped at app.$workspaceId.inbox.tsx:15. Keep Later — that one she explicitly wants.

gaps.title: Ship the tabbed inbox to the deployed instance
gaps.ask: 'humare wale jo inbox hai — agar is pe click karte hain to humare paas sirf yeh notification layout hai. Balke teen hain...'
gaps.why: Frame 179_1129 is rundesk.theaura.agency and shows a bare 'Notifications' page: title, subtitle, '32 new', 'Mark all read', then one 'UNREAD · 32' heading and a flat list. No buckets, no chips, no Filter, no gear, no Clear all. The tab work exists on main (commits 712149a 2026-08-03 and 7233c3f 2026-08-04, rendered at workspace-inbox-page.tsx:392-433) but the build she was shown predates it — the legacy 'inbox.unread'/'inbox.earlier' keys still sitting at catalogs.ts:71-72 are that old layout's strings and are referenced by no component today. Redeploy, verify the Inbox/Later/Cleared row actually renders, and delete the dead keys.

gaps.title: Inbox settings drawer: Show All tab, Group by date, Sort by newest first, Display mode
gaps.ask: The gear on the Primary tab that opens 'Customize Inbox' — the container she goes through to reach Customize importance.
gaps.why: Our gear is a bare Link out to /app/profile?tab=notifications (workspace-inbox-page.tsx:377-385); there is no inbox-level settings surface, so 'Customize importance' has nowhere to live. Build the drawer with the four controls ClickUp shows: 'Show All tab' (hide the All chip), 'Group by date' (today the dayBucket grouping at :242-248 is unconditional), 'Sort by newest first' (today desc is hardcoded at notifications.service.ts:466 and needs an order param), and 'Display mode' Fullscreen vs Inline (today every row navigates away, :472-476 — Inline means expanding the notification in place). Footer rows link to Notification settings and the existing global Keyboard shortcuts overlay (catalogs.ts:2709).

gaps.title: Notify people when their follower/watcher status changes
gaps.ask: 'FOLLOWER CHANGE — yaani ke agar mere hi task pe koi follower add ho' — listed as an Important notification type in ClickUp's panel.
gaps.why: addWatcher and removeWatcher (apps/api/src/modules/tasks/tasks.service.ts:2784-2794) only insert/delete the row and emit a realtime `watchers.updated`; nothing is written to notifications. So you can be put on the hook for a task's whole update stream without ever being told. The watcher plumbing and the bell UI already exist (task-detail-sheet.tsx:775-788, :2708-2850) — this is one notifications.create in each method plus a `follower_change` value in packages/db/src/schema/enums.ts and a TYPE_META entry.

gaps.title: Notify on assignee change, including being removed from a task
gaps.ask: 'kisi ne mera hi task kisi aur ko de diya aur mujhe REMOVE kar diya to mujhe woh cheez show ho' — ClickUp's 'Assignee change'.
gaps.why: Being handed a task notifies you (tasks.service.ts:2740-2751), but being taken off one does not: removeAssignee (:2759-2765) logs activity and returns. notifyTaskUpdate (:224-297) also ignores assignee moves entirely — it only looks at status, priority, dueDate, title, description — so watchers never learn who a task moved to either. Add an `assignee_change` type, fire it to the removed user and to watchers, and name both ends of the move the way the status copy already does at :262-265.

gaps.title: Reaction notifications
gaps.ask: 'Ab neeche se REACTIONS mujhe na show hon' — a togglable type in ClickUp's importance list.
gaps.why: Emoji reactions exist on comments (packages/db/src/schema/comments.ts:23-29) and chat messages (packages/db/src/schema/chat.ts) and are exposed in the UI, but reacting to something never notifies its author — grep for `reaction` across apps/api/src/modules/notifications returns nothing. Needed both for parity and so that the Customize importance list has the row she toggles off in the demo.

gaps.title: 'Shared with me' notification when someone shares an item with you
gaps.ask: '[shared with] mujhe na show ho' — a togglable type in ClickUp's importance list.
gaps.why: apps/api/src/modules/shares/shares.service.ts writes the share and nothing else — grep for `notifications` in that directory returns nothing — so the only way to discover a share is to visit the Shared-with-me page (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-shared-page.tsx:77-82) and look. Emit a `shared_with_me` notification on share creation, deep-linked to the shared object, reusing the entity-type labels already at catalogs.ts:4760-4766.

gaps.title: Request-access flow for content, plus its notification
gaps.ask: 'agar ACCESS REQUEST — agar kisi ne koi access maanga to mujhe show ho'
gaps.why: There is no way to ask an owner for access to a space, list, task or doc: greps for requestAccess / 'request access' outside the integrations module return nothing, and the only access-request table is packages/db/src/schema/integration-access-requests.ts (OAuth connections). Hitting a private object today is a dead end. Needs a request button on the permission-denied path, an approvals surface for the owner, and an `access_request` notification type.

gaps.title: Give assigned comments and resolved comments their own notification types
gaps.ask: 'kisi ne mujhe comment/assign kiya to mujhe show ho' — ClickUp lists 'Assigned comments' and 'Resolved comments' as separately togglable rows.
gaps.why: Both notifications fire but wear someone else's type: assignComment sends `task_assigned` (tasks.service.ts:2996-3010) and notifyCommentResolved sends `task_commented` (:3055-3098). In the inbox they are indistinguishable from a task assignment and a new comment, and in Customize importance they could never be toggled independently — which is precisely the granularity ClickUp's panel sells (Resolved comments defaults to Not Important while New comments defaults to Important). Add `comment_assigned` and `comment_resolved` types and switch the two call sites.

gaps.title: 'Task created' / 'Subtask created' notification types
gaps.ask: Rows in ClickUp's Customize importance list, defaulted to Not Important.
gaps.why: Neither exists in packages/db/src/schema/enums.ts:73-96 nor in the NotificationType union at apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notifications.service.ts:142-157, so nothing is written when a task or subtask appears in a list you follow. Cheap to add once the importance map exists — they ship off by default, which is exactly why they belong in the 'Not Important' half of the panel rather than being omitted.

gaps.title: 'Clear all' bulk action on the inbox
gaps.ask: Visible top-right of ClickUp's inbox toolbar in every frame of this section, beside the gear.
gaps.why: Clearing is one row at a time — the inbox issues a separate POST /notifications/:id/clear per notification (workspace-inbox-page.tsx:308-312). The only bulk control we ship is 'Mark all read' (:365-373), which is a different verb: read does not move a row out of the Inbox bucket. With 32 unread on the demo account there is no way to empty the list. Add a bulk clear endpoint scoped to the current bucket + filter, and mirror the confirm-then-act pattern already used in trash-tab.tsx:153-159.

gaps.title: 'Filter' control on the inbox
gaps.ask: The funnel-icon 'Filter' button at the left of ClickUp's inbox toolbar.
gaps.why: We have no filtering beyond the three chips: the inbox page renders no filter control, and GET /notifications accepts only `unreadOnly` and `view` (apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notifications.controller.ts list()). Once notification volume is real, 'show me only mentions from Hamda in this space' is the difference between an inbox and a wall. Wants filters on type, actor, workspace/space and read-state, wired through the existing view query.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Hovering (or clicking) any message in a channel or DM floats a compact pill-shaped action bar anchored to the top-right of that message row. It is the single entry point for every per-message action; the row itself also gets a subtle background tint while hovered.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Left→right, with thin vertical dividers between groups: (1) three one-click quick reactions rendered as real emoji — 👍, ✅, 🔥; (2) 😀+ "add reaction" opening the full emoji picker; | (3) curved left arrow = Reply (opens thread); (4) up-arrow-out-of-tray = Forward; (5) bookmark = Save for later; (6) person-with-arrow = Assign; (7) purple check-circle-with-sparkle = Create Task; (8) multicolour sparkle = AI/Brain; (9) "…" overflow menu. Same toolbar and same order appears on channel messages and on DM messages (frames 225, 232, 236, 242).

clickup_spec.behaviour: Clicking 😀+ in the hover toolbar opens the complete emoji library — the consultant explicitly calls out "poori ki poori emoji icons ki list" ([14:21]). The three leading emoji in the toolbar (👍 ✅ 🔥) are one-tap shortcuts that add that reaction without opening the picker.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Quick reactions are drawn as the actual coloured emoji glyphs, not monochrome icons. The picker is a full searchable/categorised emoji list, not a handful of presets.

clickup_spec.behaviour: The reply arrow opens a right-hand Thread panel scoped to that message. The consultant contrasts this with replying in the composer: a normal reply lands in the channel's main flow, whereas replying here lands inside that message's thread and renders below the original message ([14:37]–[14:48]). The channel URL gains a /t/<messageId> segment so a thread is deep-linkable.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Panel title is "<FirstName>'s Thread" (e.g. "Hamda's Thread"), not a generic "Thread". X close button top-right. Directly under the title, a two-button row: "Assign to" (person-with-arrow icon) and "Create Task ⌄" (purple check-circle-sparkle icon, with a dropdown chevron). Horizontal rule. Parent message shown with avatar, author name, time, body. Then a left-aligned divider label "No replies" when empty, or "1 Reply" / "N Replies" once replies exist. Reply composer at the bottom with placeholder "Reply, press 'space' for AI, '/' for commands", an unchecked checkbox "Also send to #General", and a "…" overflow, microphone and split send button.

clickup_spec.feature: Inline thread indicator on the parent message
clickup_spec.behaviour: Once a message has replies, a compact indicator renders under it in the channel; clicking it opens the thread panel.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Two variants seen: hovered state shows "[replier avatar] 1 reply   View thread" with a right-chevron ">" at the far right of the row (frame 232); resting state shows "[replier avatar] 1 reply   Today at 5:37 PM" (frames 237, 242). The count and the last-reply timestamp are both surfaced.

clickup_spec.behaviour: The forward icon opens a modal, not an inline menu. You pick a recipient (person or channel), optionally attach your own covering note, and send. A "Copy link" escape hatch in the same modal yields a permalink to the message instead of forwarding it. Forward stays disabled until a recipient is chosen.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Modal title "Forward this message", X to close. Search input with magnifier, placeholder "Choose a user or Channel". Textarea below, placeholder "Write a message (optional)". Then a read-only quoted preview of the message being forwarded — left vertical rule, original author avatar, author name, body. Footer: "Copy link" (left, secondary) and "Forward" (right, primary, greyed until valid).

clickup_spec.behaviour: After forwarding, a toast confirms and offers to jump to the destination conversation ([15:00]–[15:03]).
clickup_spec.ui_details: Bottom-left toast: green check icon + "Your message has been forwarded" with a "View" button. Clicking through lands in the recipient DM, where a jump pill "↑ 1 new message" with an X appears above the red "New" unread divider.

clickup_spec.behaviour: A forwarded message is not pasted text — it arrives as a structured envelope: the forwarder is the message author, and the original message is nested inside as a quote carrying its own author, original timestamp and body, plus provenance back to where it came from ([15:03]).
clickup_spec.ui_details: Outer header "Hamda Tahir  5:38 PM". Inside a left-rule quote block: nested header "[avatar] You   Today at 5:37 pm" (the original author, rendered as "You" when it is the viewer) and the body "can we communicate". Footer line inside the block: "Forwarded from #General · View message", where "View message" is a blue hyperlink that deep-links to the source message in the source channel.

clickup_spec.feature: Save a message for later (bookmark / star)
clickup_spec.behaviour: The bookmark icon saves the message to a personal "later" list. The consultant frames it as WhatsApp's star and Instagram/YouTube "saved reels" — a way to pull an important message back out of a long chat you could never scroll ([15:07]–[15:22], [15:42]–[15:47]).
clickup_spec.ui_details: On save: the bookmark icon in the toolbar becomes filled/active; the message row is tinted a warm cream/amber; and an inline badge appears in the message header next to the timestamp — "Hamda Tahir  5:37 PM  ·  🔖 Later" with a brown bookmark glyph and the literal word "Later". clickup_spec.feature: Saved messages surface in Inbox → Later

gaps.title: Forwarded messages carry no provenance — no original author, no source channel, no "View message" link
gaps.ask: Forward a message and, on the receiving side, the message should arrive as a quoted card showing who originally wrote it and when, with a footer "Forwarded from #General · View message" that jumps back to the source message.
gaps.why: Rundesk's forward posts a brand-new message whose body is literally `"Forwarded message:\n" + original body` (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:2013-2016). The recipient sees the forwarder as the author, loses the original author and timestamp entirely, cannot tell which channel it came from, and has no way to open the source. There is no column for it either — packages/db/src/schema/chat.ts:52-68 has no forwardedFrom* field. The prefix is also hardcoded English, so it is untranslated in the other three catalogs. This is the single most load-bearing miss in the section: it turns forwarding from a citation into a copy-paste.

gaps.title: Forward is a 10-item dropdown, not a "Forward this message" modal
gaps.ask: Clicking Forward should open a modal with a searchable "Choose a user or Channel" field, a "Write a message (optional)" note box, a preview of the message being forwarded, a "Copy link" button and a "Forward" confirm button that stays disabled until a recipient is picked.
gaps.why: Today the button toggles an inline popover listing `[...publicChannels, ...dmChannels].slice(0, 10)` (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:2004-2023). No search, so any workspace with more than ten conversations physically cannot forward to the eleventh. No covering note, no preview, no confirm step — one stray click forwards immediately and irreversibly.

gaps.title: Saved chat messages never reach Inbox → Later
gaps.ask: Save a message, then go to Inbox → "Later" and find it there under a "Saved" heading, with the tab showing a "1 Saved" sub-count and each row reading "Saved in #General".
gaps.why: Rundesk's Later tab is defined server-side as notifications with a future snoozedUntil (apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notifications.service.ts:438-439, counts at :563-566) and it deliberately expires (:527). Chat saves live in a completely disjoint table (packages/db/src/schema/chat.ts:142-158) surfaced only in a chat-page side panel (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:2660-2745). Grepping apps/api/src for chatMessageSaves outside the chat module returns nothing — the two systems have never been joined. Result: a user who saves a message and leaves Chat has no Inbox path back to it, which is exactly the WhatsApp-star retrieval loop the consultant is describing.

gaps.title: A saved message shows no persistent marker — no toast, no "Later" badge, no row tint
gaps.ask: Saving should confirm itself: a toast "Message saved for later" with a link into Later, an inline "🔖 Later" badge next to the message timestamp, and a warm tint on the saved row so you can spot it while scrolling the channel.
gaps.why: setSavedMutation.onSuccess only invalidates the query cache (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:1051-1053) — no toast, unlike every sibling mutation in the file (:877, :920, :1055). The message header render (:1808-1831) has a "Pinned" badge branch but nothing for saved, and `savedIds` is read only at :2027-2033 to tint the hover-toolbar icon, which vanishes on mouse-out. So after saving, the UI gives back nothing you can see.

gaps.title: No "Set reminder" on a saved message — reminders cannot attach to chat
gaps.ask: The save confirmation should offer "Set reminder", so an important message can nudge you at a chosen time rather than sitting silently in a list.
gaps.why: reminders.taskId is NOT NULL (packages/db/src/schema/reminders.ts:13-30), so a reminder can only hang off a task. The chat /remind slash command already has to work around this by fabricating a task first (apps/api/src/modules/chat/chat.service.ts:1831-1843, comment: "Back the reminder with a task carrying its text"). Supporting message reminders needs the subject to become nullable or polymorphic; it is not a UI-only change.

gaps.title: Emoji picker offers 6 emoji, not the full library
gaps.ask: Clicking the add-reaction button should open the whole emoji list — "poori ki poori emoji icons ki list" — searchable and categorised.
gaps.why: The reaction picker is a hardcoded six: `['😀','🔥','❤️','👏','👍','🎉']` (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:1906); the composer's picker is a hardcoded twelve (apps/web/src/components/chat/chat-composer.tsx:35 COMMON_EMOJIS). There is no emoji-picker library in the web app's dependencies. The reaction plumbing behind it is complete (schema chat.ts:110-116, POST /chat/messages/:messageId/reactions at chat.controller.ts:365, reactor-name tooltips at workspace-chat-page.tsx:2097-2106) — this is purely the picker UI.

gaps.title: Only one quick reaction (👍) in the hover toolbar, and it is drawn as an icon not an emoji
gaps.ask: The toolbar should lead with three one-tap emoji reactions — 👍 ✅ 🔥 — rendered as the actual emoji.
gaps.why: apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:1971-1983 has a single button using the lucide `ThumbsUp` glyph. The thread panel already does the right thing with three real emoji (:3281-3293), so the pattern exists and just needs to be lifted into the channel row — ideally with the trio configurable rather than hardcoded.

gaps.title: No permalink to an individual message ("Copy link") and no /t/<messageId> route
gaps.ask: Every message should have a copyable link that opens that message in its channel — the same link the Forward modal offers via "Copy link" and that "View message" resolves to.
gaps.why: Copy link exists only at channel level (apps/web/src/components/chat/chat-header.tsx:95, :258-260). The chat route takes no message segment (apps/web/src/routes/app.$workspaceId.chat.lazy.tsx), so there is nothing to copy. This blocks the forward-provenance work above and the "View message" link, so it is worth doing first.

gaps.title: Thread panel header has no "Assign to" / "Create Task" buttons, and is titled generically
gaps.ask: Opening a thread should show "<Author>'s Thread" with "Assign to" and "Create Task ⌄" sitting right under the title, so you can turn the conversation into work without leaving the panel.
gaps.why: The ThreadPanel header renders only the title, a followers count and an X (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:3305-3321), and the title is the generic t('chat.thread') = "Thread" (:3309). Create-task-from-message is fully built (dialog at :1574-1635, POST /chat/messages/:messageId/create-task at apps/api/src/modules/chat/chat.controller.ts:243) — it is only unreachable from here. So this is mostly a re-placement, plus a real assign.

gaps.title: "Assign" on a message does not assign anything
gaps.ask: The person-with-arrow action on a message should assign that message to someone as an action item — the consultant lists assign among the things you can do to a saved message ([15:36]).
gaps.why: The button labelled t('chat.assignOpenProfile') = "Assign / Open profile" merely appends `<@authorId>` to the composer (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:2051-2060); the profile panel's Assign button does the same (:2491, :3437). The only real assignment path is arming an action item that applies to the NEXT message you send (:255, :687-691, :2278-2311), which is a different thing entirely. A user clicking Assign expecting ClickUp's behaviour gets a mention token in their draft.

gaps.title: Saved messages cannot be edited or assigned from the saved surface
gaps.ask: From the saved item you should be able to edit the message, assign it, and open its thread — all three, without navigating back into the channel.
gaps.why: SavedMessageCard (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:2748-2836) offers only tag add/remove, "Remove" and "Open thread". Editing is inline-in-channel only and gated to your own messages (:1834-1873); assign is the no-op above. Note that ClickUp's Later card also carries reaction affordances (thumbs-up, add-reaction) and a "1 reply" jump in its footer, plus Details / Clear / snooze / mark-unread in its header — none of which have an equivalent here.

gaps.title: No "…" overflow menu on the message toolbar; the right-click menu carries only 3 items
gaps.ask: The message action bar should end in a "…" that opens the long tail of actions, so the visible bar stays short.
gaps.why: Rundesk instead shows up to twelve buttons inline (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:1890-2088) and hides a separate, much smaller set behind right-click (:1533-1569 — only Create task, Mark unread, Reply). Discoverability is inverted: the crowded bar is what you see, and right-click, which nobody tries, holds a strict subset.

gaps.title: Empty channel shows a bare headline instead of onboarding action cards
gaps.ask: A new channel should offer "+ Add People", "Import from Slack", and cards for "Track Tasks", "Add Doc" and "Start SyncUp" (DM variant: "View Calendar", "Start SyncUp").
gaps.why: apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:1730-1738 renders only an icon plus "Welcome to #{{name}}" and "This is the beginning of your conversation. Send a message to get started." Add People exists as a separate dialog (apps/web/src/components/chat/add-people-dialog.tsx) but is not offered here. "Import from Slack" does not exist at all — grepping slack across apps/web/src, apps/api/src and packages returns only the outgoing Slack webhook integration (catalogs.ts:1022, :2993-2997). "Start SyncUp" has no match either (grepped syncup / huddle / 'voice call' in catalogs.ts — zero hits). Flagging the cards as one small item; Slack import and SyncUp are large and likely belong to the integrations and meetings workstreams rather than to chat.

clickup_spec.feature: Inbox tab strip (All / Primary / Other / Later / Cleared)
clickup_spec.behaviour: The notification Inbox is one page with five top tabs, each driven by a ?tab= query param (?tab=later, ?tab=cleared observed). Switching tabs re-filters the same list; the tab persists in the URL so it is linkable and survives reload.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Left→right order with a leading icon on each: 'All' (grid), 'Primary' (tray), 'Other' (pulse), 'Later' (clock), 'Cleared' (double-tick). The active tab is boxed/outlined with a thick underline bar. Only 'Later' carries a second line — a count sub-label reading '1 Saved'. The other tabs show no count.

clickup_spec.feature: Inbox toolbar: Filter, settings, Clear all
clickup_spec.behaviour: A single toolbar row sits between the tab strip and the list. 'Clear all' bulk-clears every notification in the current view in one click — 'Maine sab clear kiye — woh yahan pe chale jayenge' — moving them into the Cleared tab rather than deleting them.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Left: a bordered 'Filter' button with a funnel icon. Right, in order: a gear/settings icon button (no label), then 'Clear all' with a double-tick icon. Both right-side controls are present on every tab including Cleared and Later.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Clearing is not deletion — a cleared notification lands in the Cleared tab and stays retrievable for 30 days, then is permanently deleted automatically. Anything left in Primary/Inbox is never auto-deleted; the 30-day clock starts only at the moment of clearing ('jaise hi aap ne clear kar diya, 30 days tak rahega aur delete ho jayega'). Same contract as the Trash.
clickup_spec.ui_details: A full-width info banner is pinned to the top of the Cleared tab, above the list/empty state: an ⓘ icon, the sentence 'Cleared notifications are permanently deleted from your Inbox after 30 days.', and a bordered 'Learn more' button inside the banner on the right. The banner renders even when the tab is empty.

clickup_spec.behaviour: When a tab has nothing in it, ClickUp shows a celebratory empty state rather than a bare list.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Centred line-art illustration: an open envelope carrying a green check badge, surrounded by floating rounded cards (a red-dot card, a purple '#' card, a blue doc/pencil card, an orange speech-bubble card) linked by dotted curves. Single headline beneath: "You've achieved Inbox Zero!" — no sub-copy and no CTA button. The 30-day banner still shows above it on the Cleared tab.

clickup_spec.behaviour: 'Later' is not a snooze timer — it is the bucket for chat messages a user has bookmarked with the 'Later' flag. Flagging a message in a channel (the '🔖 Later' chip on the message) makes it appear under Inbox → Later, and the tab's sub-count reflects how many are saved.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Tab reads 'Later' with sub-label '1 Saved'. List is grouped under a bold section header 'Saved'. Each row is: bookmark icon + 'Saved in #General - Leo' (channel + workspace), then the author's avatar, then the message preview text ('can we communicate'). In the channel itself the same message shows an inline '🔖 Later' chip next to the timestamp, and so does the thread panel's parent block.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Deleted items sit in Trash for 30 days and are then auto-deleted; before that window closes the user can restore them back into the system ('agar chahiye to aap us ko wapas le aao system mein'). She calls this the same model the cleared-notification retention follows.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Described verbally at [16:27]–[16:37]; the Trash screen itself is not shown in this section's frames.

clickup_spec.behaviour: A dedicated route at /chat/r/threads that aggregates every chat thread you follow, so a person in 10 or 90 groups never has to open each channel to check whether a reply landed. A new reply arrives under Unread; once read, the thread moves to the Read tab. The page is a first-class sidebar destination, second in the Home nav directly under Inbox.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Sidebar entry 'Replies' with a curved-reply arrow icon, positioned between 'Inbox' and 'Skills'. Page heading 'Replies'; two sub-tabs directly under it — 'Unread' (default) and 'Read'; the active one is underlined. The Read tab is addressable as ?tab=read. No Filter button, no gear, no Clear all on this page.

gaps.ask: Replies should be the one place you check for thread replies across every channel — 'ek person 90 chats mein hai, 90 groups mein hai … ab us ko har baar chat open karne ki zaroorat nahi ke woh dekhe ke is mein reply aaya ya nahi. Woh yahan pe aaye, us ko yahan notification ho jaye — acha, yeh unread message hai.'
gaps.why: Rundesk's Replies page filters the notification feed to `['task_commented','doc_commented']` only (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-replies-page.tsx:24,65), so a chat thread reply — the exact case demoed in frames 274/277 — is structurally impossible to see there. On the API side a thread reply is not treated as a reply at all: apps/api/src/modules/chat/chat.service.ts:1654-1686 fans out `task_mentioned` / `chat_message` to every channel member with no branch on `parentMessageId`, so the person who actually started the thread gets the same generic 'New message in #General' as everyone else. Needs a `chat_reply` notification type dispatched to the thread's participants, plus a Replies query that groups those by parent message.

gaps.title: Replies rows are link-outs, not inline threads with a reply box
gaps.ask: Read and answer a thread from the Replies list itself: parent message, '1 Reply', the reply, and a composer with an 'Also send to #General' checkbox — 'maine aap ko conversation mein reply kiya tha … agar aap bhi yahan reply karte ho'.
gaps.why: apps/web/src/pages/workspace-replies-page.tsx:127-186 renders a flat Card per notification whose onClick navigates away; the only control is 'Resolve'. ClickUp (frames 277, 282) renders the amber parent block, a '1 Reply' divider, each reply, and a full composer with placeholder "Reply, press 'space' for AI, '/' for commands", an 'Also send to #General' checkbox, a '⋯' overflow, a mic and a send-with-'˅'. The whole point is not opening the channel — a link-out defeats it. The composer already exists and can be lifted: apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:3353-3378 (`ThreadReplyComposer` + 'chat.alsoSendToChannel').

gaps.title: Cleared notifications are never purged — no 30-day retention
gaps.ask: 'after 30 DAYS baad woh saare notifications automatically VANISH ho jayenge … jaise hi aap ne clear kar diya, 30 days tak rahega aur delete ho jayega' — clearing starts a 30-day clock, exactly like Trash.
gaps.why: `clear()` only stamps `dismissedAt` (apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notifications.service.ts:582-588) and nothing ever deletes the row — no `@Cron` in apps/api/src/modules/notifications/ does a delete, and there is no `delete(notifications)` anywhere in apps/api/src. Cleared rows therefore accumulate forever and the Cleared tab count grows without bound. The pattern to copy is already written: apps/api/src/modules/trash/trash.service.ts:14 (`TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS = 30`) and :317-330 (`@Cron(EVERY_DAY_AT_4AM) purgeExpired()`). Index `idx_notifications_user_triage` (packages/db/src/schema/notifications.ts:26) already covers `dismissedAt`.

gaps.title: No 30-day retention banner on the Cleared tab — and current copy promises the opposite
gaps.ask: Tell the user, on the Cleared tab, that these will be permanently deleted after 30 days, with a way to read more.
gaps.why: ClickUp pins an ⓘ banner above the list on ?tab=cleared reading exactly 'Cleared notifications are permanently deleted from your Inbox after 30 days.' with a bordered 'Learn more' button (frames 261, 266, 271, 273) — it renders even when the tab is empty. Rundesk renders no banner (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-inbox-page.tsx:436-499) and its Cleared empty state actively contradicts the contract: apps/web/src/lib/i18n/catalogs.ts:4662 'inbox.emptyClearedDesc' = 'Cleared notifications stay here in case you need one back.' Ship this with the purge job or the copy will be a lie in the other direction. Mirror apps/web/src/components/trash-tab.tsx:145 / 'trash.retentionNotice' (catalogs.ts:3744) and localise into all four catalogs (en/es/ar/ur).

gaps.title: No 'Clear all' bulk action on the Inbox
gaps.ask: 'mere paas jitne bhi notifications hain main yahan se clear kar sakti hoon. Maine sab clear kiye — woh yahan pe chale jayenge' — one button that clears the whole view into Cleared.
gaps.why: ClickUp's inbox toolbar carries a gear icon and a 'Clear all' button (double-tick icon) on the right of every tab (frames 256, 261, 271). Rundesk's header (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-inbox-page.tsx:359-386) offers only 'Mark all read' — a different verb that leaves everything in the Inbox — and clearing is per-row only (:600-608). The API has `mark-all-read` (apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notifications.controller.ts:110) but no bulk clear; the frontend currently fires one POST per id (:308-312), which would be a request storm at 200 notifications. Needs POST /notifications/clear-all scoped to the active view+filter.

gaps.title: Saved chat messages don't appear in the Inbox 'Later' tab
gaps.ask: Flag a message '🔖 Later' in a channel and find it under Inbox → Later, listed under a 'Saved' header as 'Saved in #General - Leo' with the message preview, with the tab showing '1 Saved'.
gaps.quote_ts: 15:51 (frame 256; Later tab is the tab she is leaving as the section opens)
gaps.why: Both halves exist and are disconnected. Rundesk's Later bucket is purely snooze-driven (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-inbox-page.tsx:67-72, 609-635; apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notifications.service.ts:604-618 keyed on `snoozedUntil`), while message bookmarks live in a separate per-user table (packages/db/src/schema/chat.ts:141-156 `chatMessageSaves`) surfaced only in a chat-side 'Saved' panel (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:2689). Result: no 'Saved' section header, no 'Saved in #channel' row, and no 'N Saved' sub-count on the Later tab. Also needs the inline '🔖 Later' chip on the message row in chat and in the thread panel's parent block.

gaps.title: 'Replies' is not in the sidebar — only reachable from the command palette
gaps.ask: Replies sits second in the Home sidebar, right under Inbox, and is where the user goes instead of opening 10 channels.
gaps.quote_ts: 16:41 (frame 273, cursor moving onto the sidebar 'Replies' entry) and 17:21
gaps.why: apps/web/src/components/workspace-sidebar.tsx:117-134 (`workspaceNavEntries`) omits Replies entirely, and the dock at :1377 links only /inbox. The single nav reference in the whole app is apps/web/src/components/command-palette.tsx:296. A feature nobody can find is a feature nobody has — and it is a one-line fix that unblocks the value of every other Replies item above.

gaps.title: No 'Mark unread' for a notification or a reply thread
gaps.ask: 'agar to maine READ kiya hai to yeh is tarah se chala jayega' — read moves it to the Read tab; the 'Mark unread' button on the thread header pushes it back to Unread.
gaps.why: The read→Read-tab half works (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-replies-page.tsx:65-68, 133-137), but the reverse does not exist for notifications: apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notifications.controller.ts exposes only `:id/read` (:102) and `mark-all-read` (:110) — there is no `unread` route and no service method to null out `readAt`. Chat already has 'Mark unread' / 'Mark unread from here' for channels and messages (apps/web/src/lib/i18n/catalogs.ts:4799-4801; apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:1548-1556, 3296), so the concept is established — it just doesn't cross over to the Replies/Inbox surfaces where ClickUp renders it as a bordered header button (frames 277, 282).

gaps.title: No per-thread mute or follow/unfollow
gaps.ask: The Replies thread header carries a mute-thread (bell-with-slash) icon and a bookmark icon next to 'Mark unread', so a noisy thread in one of your 10 groups can be silenced without leaving the channel.
gaps.why: Muting in Rundesk is channel-wide only ('chat.mute' at apps/web/src/lib/i18n/catalogs.ts:3050; enforced via `levelByUser` 'all'|'mentions'|'none' at apps/api/src/modules/chat/chat.service.ts:1646,1671), which is too blunt — muting the channel kills the messages you do want. There is no thread-follower table either: followers are derived at render time from the parent author plus repliers (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:3247-3255), so 'stop following this thread' has nothing to persist to. Needs a `chat_thread_follows` table (following/muted per user per parent message) before the header icons in frames 277/282 can be built.

gaps.title: Thread panel header lacks the name and the Assign to / Create Task row
gaps.ask: The thread panel is titled "Hamda's Thread" and puts 'Assign to' and 'Create Task' directly under the title.
gaps.why: apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:3308 renders a generic 'Thread' title with the follower count beneath, and no action row — create-task and assign-action-item exist but are buried in the per-message hover menu (:1542 'chat.createTaskFromMessage', :2278 'chat.assignActionItem'). Purely a surfacing change: name the panel after the parent author and promote the two existing actions into the header. Small, cosmetic, and cheap next to the items above.

clickup_spec.feature: Skills as a first-class sidebar destination
clickup_spec.behaviour: "Skills" is a top-level item in the Home sidebar, between "Replies" and "Meetings", with a gem/diamond icon. Clicking it routes to /{workspaceId}/ai/skills?sidebar=home — i.e. Skills lives under the AI namespace but is reachable in one click from Home. The browser tab title becomes "Ask AI | {workspace}".
clickup_spec.ui_details: Sidebar order: Inbox, Replies, Skills, Meetings, My Tasks, "⋯ More". Selected item gets a filled/rounded highlight. Hover shows the target URL in the browser status bar.

clickup_spec.behaviour: The hub page has a title "Skills" on the left of the header and a primary black "+ New Skill" button on the far right. Body is two stacked regions: a horizontally scrolling starter carousel on top, and the skills library (tabs + toolbar + list) below.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Header row: "Skills" (h1, left) … "+ New Skill" (solid dark button, right). Carousel has a circular ">" chevron pinned to its right edge for paging; cards are fixed width and clip at the viewport edge.

clickup_spec.feature: Skill starter carousel — mining, discovery and scratch cards
clickup_spec.behaviour: Three functional starter cards sit first in the carousel. "Skills Miner" scans your existing work to propose skills worth saving. "For your team" scans the workspace to surface skills other people already created. "New Skill" starts an empty skill.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Card 1 — eyebrow "Skills Miner" (person+magnifier icon); title "Turn repeat work into skills"; body "Scan your tasks, docs, and chats to surface workflows worth saving."; footer button with magnifier icon: "Find my Skills". Card 2 — eyebrow "For your team" (people icon); title "Discover team skills"; body "Discover skills created across your workspace."; button "Scan my workspace". Card 3 — eyebrow "New Skill" (gem icon); title "Start from scratch"; body "Package your expertise into a reusable skill"; button "+ Create skill". Cards 1–3 have a neutral/white background; the footer button is a full-width outlined pill.

clickup_spec.behaviour: After the three functional cards the carousel continues with prebuilt, opinionated skill templates. Each is a coloured card that, on "+ Create skill", starts an interview-style setup for that skill archetype.
clickup_spec.ui_details: "Delegate Like Me" — coral/red gradient card, person-badge icon — "Assigns and hands off work the way you would". "Brand Voice" — green gradient card, check-badge icon — "Interviews you on tone, terminology, and audience for your brand". "Triage Tasks Like Me" — blue gradient card, check-badge icon — "Prioritizes and sorts incoming … you usually would". Each ends in a "+ Create skill" pill. More templates exist beyond the right edge (the ">" chevron).

clickup_spec.feature: Skills library — tabs, filters and view toggles
clickup_spec.behaviour: Below the carousel the saved skills are listed, scoped by three tabs and refined with a filter/search/state toolbar, viewable as a table or a grid.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Tabs left-aligned: "All Skills" (active, underlined), "Enabled" (check-circle icon), "Created by me" (person icon). Right-aligned icon toolbar in order: filter/sliders, magnifier (search), check-circle (enabled-state filter), then a segmented pair of view toggles — table/list view and grid view. Implies each skill row carries an enabled/disabled state and an owner.

clickup_spec.behaviour: With no skills saved the library area shows a centred illustration and a call to action; the same "+ Create skill" affordance repeats here so an empty workspace has two ways in.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Centred gem icon in a rounded tile; headline "Skills teach Brain how you work"; body "Turn a repetitive workflow into a skill that Brain reuses, so you never explain it again."; outlined button "+ Create skill".

clickup_spec.feature: AI authors the skill for you (chat side panel)
clickup_spec.behaviour: A right-hand AI chat panel opens beside the Skills hub without leaving the page. The user asks "Help me create a skill"; Brain explains what a skill is, recommends specific skills based on the user's actual workspace, and offers to author one. Before creating anything it states its intended design and asks for approval.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Panel occupies ~1/3 width; the Skills hub reflows to the remaining space rather than being covered. Assistant answer: "Skills are reusable playbooks that teach Brain how to handle a repeated workflow in your preferred way, consistently." then "For you, I'd start with a Personal Task Organizer, a Communication Polisher for clear en-US messages, and a Weekly Review skill that summarizes progress and plans next steps. Browse or create them in the Skills Hub." — "Skills Hub" is a hyperlink back to the page. Approval gate wording: "Approve this approach and I'll create it, or tell me one tweak you want first." (bolded). Grounded on real data: "I found a mostly empty personal list, so I'd keep this simple and low-maintenance…".

clickup_spec.feature: Visible reasoning trace while the model works
clickup_spec.behaviour: While generating, the assistant shows a "Pondering" label and then streams the retrieval/reasoning steps it is running, before the answer text appears.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Multicolour brain avatar + status word "Pondering". Beneath it, bulleted steps appear one at a time in muted text: "Checking what you're working on", "Checking the latest Skills basics". The final answer then streams in below, and the status word is replaced by the assistant name "Brain".

clickup_spec.behaviour: A new chat starts as "New Chat"; once there is enough content the thread is renamed automatically from its topic and appears in the sidebar's "AI Chats" list, so it survives navigation and can be reopened.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Panel title chip goes "New Chat" → "Skill Definition and Ideas ˅" (chevron opens a thread menu). Sidebar "AI Chats" section shows "Skill Definition and Ideas" at the top of the list ahead of the generic "New Conversation" entries; a compose/edit icon next to the section header starts a new one. The named thread is still listed after the panel is closed.

clickup_spec.feature: Follow-up suggestion chips after each answer
clickup_spec.behaviour: Every assistant answer is followed by context-specific next actions the user can click instead of typing. Clicking one sends it as the next user message.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Section label "Follow ups" in muted text, then full-width rounded chips each prefixed with an ↳ arrow: "Create a Personal Task Organizer skill for me", "Turn my messages into a reusable Communication Polisher skill", "Find my recurring workflows and recommend the best skill". Hover raises the chip background.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Each assistant message carries a row of actions to reuse or grade the output.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Six icons in order: copy (duplicate squares), check-circle (create task from this), document-with-arrow (save to doc), loop (regenerate/try again), thumbs-up, thumbs-down.

clickup_spec.feature: AI composer — context chip, model picker, attach, stop/send, mic
clickup_spec.behaviour: The composer scopes the conversation to a context ("Skills") and lets the user pick the model tier. While a response streams the send control becomes a stop button and the placeholder reports progress; when idle it is a send arrow with a mic beside it.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Bottom row left-to-right: "+" attach button; a chip "Skills" with a brain icon (the active context/tool scope); right side: model selector "Max ˅" with brain icon; then a filled circular stop button (square glyph) while streaming, or a mic icon + blue circular send arrow when idle. Placeholder while streaming: "Working on it…". Typed example: "project management task assigning".

clickup_spec.behaviour: A skill has a Memory: everything discussed with it is stored inside the skill, so it accumulates context about how you work and does not need re-explaining. (Described verbally at 18:42–18:58; the on-screen surface is not opened in these frames.)
clickup_spec.ui_details: Not shown on screen in this section — spoken only: "Yeh MEMORY hai — yeh hum jo bhi baat karenge woh STORE karega apne andar." Consistent with the hub copy "a skill that Brain reuses, so you never explain it again."

clickup_spec.behaviour: A built skill can be connected outward to any other system, so the skill executes against external tools rather than only inside the product. (Described verbally at 18:58–19:07.)
clickup_spec.ui_details: Not shown on screen in this section — spoken only: "Aur yeh CONNECTIONS hai — agar main is ko build karoongi to main is ko kisi bhi system mein CONNECT kar sakti hoon."

clickup_spec.feature: Positioning — a skill is not a feature
clickup_spec.behaviour: The consultant closes by insisting on the vocabulary: what is added to the workspace is a SKILL, not a feature — an agent that does the work you do, to the point that "aap REPLACE ho sakte ho".
clickup_spec.ui_details: Naming matters for our build: the nav item, page title, primary button and empty state must all say "Skill(s)", never "prompt", "template" or "automation".

gaps.title: Skills: a library of named, reusable AI playbooks (page, schema, API, nav)

No transcription/ASR provider anywhere in apps/api/src/modules/ai/ (grep 'meeting' there returns only the paste-notes extractor at ai.service.ts:957-961 and ai.controller.ts:192).
rundesk_status.notes: The `meetings.transcript` column (packages/db/src/schema/meetings.ts:33) and extractActionItems' transcript fallback (meetings.service.ts:340) already exist — the storage half of AI Notes is in place, the capture half is not.

rundesk_status.feature: Admin gate for a paid meeting-AI capability
rundesk_status.evidence: Feature flags for both already exist as toggles: catalogs.ts:1432 'adminFeatures.flag.ai.meeting_notes': 'Meeting Notes' and :1472 'adminFeatures.flag.integrations.meetings': 'Meetings', surfaced on apps/web/src/pages/admin-features-page.tsx.
rundesk_status.notes: Matches her point that recording has to be switched on 'back end se'. What is missing is the user-facing upsell path — no 'Contact your admin' modal exists when a gated feature is touched.

rundesk_status.feature: Create an external Zoom / Google Meet meeting from a task
rundesk_status.evidence: apps/api/src/modules/tasks/meetings.controller.ts:11-21 (POST /tasks/:taskId/meeting {provider}; POST /tasks/:taskId/meeting/:linkId/recording). UI: apps/web/src/components/task-detail-sheet.tsx:1762-1848 (Zoom / Google Meet buttons, disabled with 'Connect this provider in Integrations to create meetings.'), recording attach at :2035-2058. Strings catalogs.ts:3891-3899.
rundesk_status.notes: Rundesk's answer to 'jump on a call' today is to send you to Zoom/Meet. That is not the same product as an in-app SyncUp, but it is real and should not be rebuilt.

rundesk_status.feature: Shared meetings between two people (DM Calendar tab)
rundesk_status.evidence: apps/api/src/modules/meetings/meetings.service.ts:248-322 (sharedWith — meetings both attended + open shared tasks); controller apps/api/src/modules/meetings/meetings.controller.ts:109-117; UI apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:3147-3190; strings catalogs.ts:3114-3121 ('Chat' / 'Calendar' / 'Tasks' tabs, 'Meetings with {{name}}', 'No meetings with {{name}} yet.').
rundesk_status.notes: Not shown in these frames, but it is the one place meetings already render in a list.

rundesk_status.feature: Realtime transport that a call would sit on
rundesk_status.evidence: apps/api/src/modules/realtime/realtime.gateway.ts:102-329 — socket.io WebSocketGateway with JWT auth, room subscribe/unsubscribe, presence.ping, canvas.cursor broadcast, and per-entity emit helpers (user/list/task/workspace/doc rooms). Presence at apps/api/src/modules/presence/presence.service.ts:23-40.
rundesk_status.notes: Signalling could be layered on this gateway, but there is no media plane — no SFU, no TURN config, no peer-connection code anywhere in the repo.

gaps.title: SyncUp: in-app voice/video calls started from a channel
gaps.ask: Start a call from inside the workspace the way ClickUp's SyncUp does — a call button in the channel header and a 'Start SyncUp — Jump on a voice call or video call' card in the channel, joinable by anyone in that channel. She walks the whole thing end to end and closes with 'Yeh poora ka poora [call] feature hai.'
gaps.why: Rundesk has no calling of any kind. grep across apps/ and packages/ for syncup|webrtc|getUserMedia|getDisplayMedia|RTCPeerConnection|livekit|jitsi|agora matches only apps/web/src/pages/workspace-clips-page.tsx; grep for huddle|startCall|videoCall|voiceCall|joinCall across apps/web/src and apps/api/src returns nothing; the chat page has no call icon at all. Today the product's answer to 'let's jump on a call' is task-detail-sheet.tsx:1826-1847, which sends you out to Zoom or Google Meet. This is the single largest item in the section and needs a media plane (SFU/TURN) that does not exist — the socket.io gateway at apps/api/src/modules/realtime/realtime.gateway.ts:102-329 can carry signalling but nothing else.

gaps.title: Pre-join preview dialog with device pickers and background effects
gaps.ask: Before joining, show a preview with camera on/off, a background/colour picker ('BACKGROUND colours wagera select down kar sakte ho'), a mic device dropdown with a live level meter, a speaker dropdown, and an 'Always show preview before joining' checkbox, with Cancel / Start SyncUp.
gaps.why: No pre-join or device-selection UI exists. Clips (apps/web/src/pages/workspace-clips-page.tsx, strings catalogs.ts:423-459) already calls getUserMedia/getDisplayMedia and handles the HTTPS/permission failure cases, so the permission plumbing is a partial precedent — but there is no camera preview, no enumerateDevices dropdowns, no level meter and no background/effects layer anywhere in the repo.

gaps.title: In-call screen share (tab / window / entire screen)
gaps.ask: From inside a call, share a browser tab, a window, or the entire screen — 'yeh mujhe poochta hai ke koi tab share karni hai, window share karni hai, ya entire screen share karni hai'.
gaps.why: Nothing streams a screen to other people. getDisplayMedia is used exactly once, in Clips, and it records to a stored file rather than a live track (catalogs.ts:452-453 'Screen recording blocked'). Depends on the SyncUp media plane.

gaps.title: Call participants panel with 'Invite people'
gaps.ask: An in-call Participants panel listing who is on the call, with an invite control that can pull in existing members and add new ones — 'main PARTICIPANT ko invite kar sakti hoon; new members ko bhi add kar sakti hoon'. Empty state reads 'You''re the only one here / Invite other people to join the SyncUp'.
gaps.why: No participants panel exists. Channel membership has 'Add people' (catalogs.ts:208) and 'Add people to #{{channel}}' (catalogs.ts:3415), but that adds someone to a channel, not to a live call. The meeting_attendees table (packages/db/src/schema/meetings.ts:50-66) is the right home for the roster once calls exist.

gaps.title: Call thread — 'Every SyncUp has a thread'
gaps.ask: A message thread attached to the call itself, so what was posted during the call survives it, with an 'Also send to #General' checkbox on each reply.
gaps.why: The exact reply UI is already built for chat threads — apps/web/src/pages/workspace-chat-page.tsx:1130-1142 and :3233-3361, string catalogs.ts:4774 'Also send to {{channel}}' — so this is mostly re-pointing an existing component at a call entity. What does not exist is the call to attach it to, or any 'Call Thread' panel.

gaps.title: In-call reactions overlay
gaps.ask: Send an emoji reaction during a call and have it show up on the call surface — 'Agar main koi reaction doongi to woh yahan pe show ho jaata hai.'
gaps.why: Chat reactions exist (she confirms 'abhi humare paas bhi hai'), but there is no call surface to render a reaction on, and no ephemeral/animated reaction broadcast. Depends on SyncUp.

gaps.title: Emoji picker: search, Frequently Used, categories, add-custom '+'
gaps.ask: The picker she opens has a 'Search...' field, a 'Frequently Used' section, a 'Smiles & People' grid, a bottom category tab strip, and a '+' to add a custom emoji inline.
gaps.why: Rundesk's picker is a hard-coded 12-emoji strip — apps/web/src/components/chat/chat-composer.tsx:35 COMMON_EMOJIS, rendered at :370. No search, no recency tracking, no categories, and no in-picker add-custom (custom emoji are managed separately, catalogs.ts:216-217, 3103). NOTE: this is a chat-surface item and may also be raised by the G11/G12 chat sections — dedupe before scheduling.

gaps.title: Minimise a running call to a docked picture-in-picture
gaps.ask: Collapse the call and keep talking while browsing — 'main THREAD ko MINIMIZE kar sakti hoon yahan se, aur phir woh is tarah se show hota hai' — a small self-view panel docked at the bottom of the sidebar with mic, camera, '⋯' and a red hang-up, plus a call indicator on the channel row.
gaps.why: Nothing like it exists; the only 'minimize' hits in apps/web/src are panel-resize icons in dashboard-widget-builder.tsx:380 and task-detail-sheet.tsx:846. Requires the call session to survive route changes (a persistent shell-level component), which is a structural decision worth making at the same time as the call itself.

gaps.title: Call cards in the channel and a call-started notification with Join
gaps.ask: When a call starts, everyone gets a notification and can join straight from it — 'aap ko notification aa raha hoga ke CALL ka option aaya… aap chaho to wahan se direct call join ho jaoge' — and the channel shows a lifecycle card: 'You''re in the SyncUp / Wait for your team to join!' + Leave, then 'SyncUp Ended / Lasted 45s · 1 person joined' with Join disabled, plus 'Join the SyncUp / No one is in the call' with Join enabled.
gaps.why: Chat has no call message type and the notification enum has no call value — packages/db/src/schema/enums.ts:73-96 lists 16 types, none call- or meeting-related. Adding a 'call_started' notification type plus a call-card message renderer is small, well-bounded work that is a prerequisite for the call being discoverable at all.

gaps.title: AI Notes: record the call and auto-generate meeting notes
gaps.ask: An 'AI Notes' toggle inside the call that, once switched on server-side, records the whole call and writes the notes for you — 'main record karoongi aur yeh aap ke khud hi NOTES bana ke dega aur poori ki poori RECORDING bhi karega — poori call hi ki. So it''s a feature that can be used in our end.'
gaps.why: Rundesk explicitly ships copy saying it does not do this: apps/web/src/lib/i18n/catalogs.ts:788 'Rundesk does not transcribe calls. Paste notes or a transcript from wherever the call was recorded.' There is no ASR/transcription provider in apps/api/src/modules/ai/ — the only meeting AI is the paste-notes extractor (ai.service.ts:957-961). The storage half is already there and should not be rebuilt: meetings.transcript and meetings.recordingUrl (packages/db/src/schema/meetings.ts:32-33) and extractActionItems' transcript fallback (meetings.service.ts:340). Needs a media recording pipeline plus a transcription vendor decision.

gaps.title: Entitlement upsell modal for gated meeting AI ('Contact your admin')
gaps.ask: Turning on a capability the workspace has not purchased should explain itself rather than fail silently: 'Unlock AI Notetaker: Automatic meeting notes connected to docs and tasks. / Contact your admin to purchase AI Meeting Notetaker for your Workspace.' + a 'Contact your admin' button. She makes the same point in her own words: recording 'back end se on karna parta hai'.
gaps.why: The admin toggles already exist — catalogs.ts:1432 'adminFeatures.flag.ai.meeting_notes' and :1472 'adminFeatures.flag.integrations.meetings', surfaced on apps/web/src/pages/admin-features-page.tsx — but there is no user-facing modal when a member hits a flag that is off; the feature simply does not render. A reusable 'gated feature' modal would pay for itself across every flag.

gaps.title: Meetings hub page and sidebar entry
gaps.ask: A 'Meetings' item in the Home sidebar (between Skills and My Tasks) opening a page where 'yahan pe aap ko show hongi meetings' — the place all meetings and their notes live.
gaps.why: No route, no page, no nav string. Verified: no app.$workspaceId.meetings*.tsx in apps/web/src/routes/, nothing in apps/web/src/pages/, no 'nav.meetings' key in catalogs.ts, and the Browse block at apps/web/src/components/workspace-sidebar.tsx:923-960 has no Meetings row. Everything meeting-shaped today is buried in the AI page's 'Meeting notes' tab (workspace-ai-page.tsx:187). The backend to feed this page already exists (GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/meetings, meetings.controller.ts:19-27), so this is mostly a front-end build.

gaps.title: Meeting notes list: Filters / My notes / Tags / Search + empty state
gaps.ask: On the meetings page, a toolbar with 'Filters', a 'My notes' pill, 'Tags:', and a right-aligned 'Search', over a list of notes; when empty, 'No Meeting Notes / Meeting Notes will appear here when AI Notetaker attends a meeting.'
gaps.why: There is no meetings list view at all — the only way to open a saved meeting is a <select> dropdown at apps/web/src/pages/workspace-ai-page.tsx:1133-1145. No filtering, no mine-vs-all, no tags on meetings (packages/db/src/schema/meetings.ts has no tag/label relation), no search. GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/meetings (meetings.service.ts:73-89) accepts only a taskId filter and caps at 200 rows with no pagination.

gaps.title: Upcoming Meetings section with Join, countdown and Connect Calendar
gaps.ask: An 'Upcoming Meetings' block with a 'Join' pill, the meeting title, a proximity badge ('in 5m'), a day timeline, and — when no calendar is connected — the 'AI Notetaker works best with Calendar / Connect your calendar to manage your events and get the most out of AI Notetaker / Connect Calendar' card, plus 'Send AI Notetaker' and 'Open Calendar' shortcuts.
gaps.why: meetings.list() has no upcoming/date-window filter and sorts newest-first (meetings.service.ts:85), and joinUrl (packages/db/src/schema/meetings.ts:31) is never rendered in apps/web. Calendar sync does exist but points elsewhere: apps/api/src/modules/calendar-sync/calendar-sync.service.ts:141-210 pulls Google/Outlook events into TASKS in an inbox list, never into `meetings`, and its UI is a settings panel (catalogs.ts:2587-2603) with no CTA on any meetings surface.

gaps.title: Meeting-scoped AI ask-box with starter prompts, and meetings in the AI/search index
gaps.ask: 'Hey {name}! Ready to dive into your meetings?' with a composer ('Get instant answers and insights from your meetings') and four chips: 'Summarize my most recent meeting notes', 'Create tasks from action items in recent meetings', 'What were the key decisions from my last meeting?', 'List all action items assigned to me from meetings'.
gaps.why: Rundesk stores meeting notes but the AI cannot see them: packages/db/src/schema/knowledge-embeddings.ts:19 restricts KnowledgeSourceType to 'task' | 'doc' | 'comment' | 'attachment', and apps/api/src/modules/search/search.service.ts:18 has no 'meeting' entity type. The existing AI chips (catalogs.ts:2697-2701) are all task/project-shaped. Only the third chip's underlying capability partly exists (action-item extraction, meetings.service.ts:332-372) and even that is per-meeting rather than 'across recent meetings'. Indexing meetings is the enabling change; the chips are cheap once it lands.

clickup_spec.behaviour: 'My Tasks' is a first-class sidebar group under Home, expandable via a disclosure triangle, with its own route (/my-work/tasks, /my-work/today). Its three children are personal work surfaces that also appear in the profile menu ('My Work').
clickup_spec.ui_details: Sidebar order: Inbox, Replies, Skills, Meetings, My Tasks, … More. Children indented under My Tasks in this exact order: 'Assigned to me' (person-in-circle icon), 'Today & Overdue' (calendar icon), 'Personal List' (person+list icon), then '… More'. Selecting a child sets the content breadcrumb to 'My Tasks / <child>'. 'Personal List' opens as a real List (URL /v/l/li/<id>) with a lock glyph in the breadcrumb, List + Board view tabs and '+ View'.

clickup_spec.behaviour: One '+ Create' / 'Add Task ⌄' entry point opens a single modal whose horizontal tab strip switches the thing being created without closing the dialog.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Tabs left→right: Task | Doc | Reminder | Whiteboard | Dashboard. Active tab is underlined. Top-right of the modal: an expand/minimize arrow and '✕'. Switching tabs keeps the modal frame; body swaps.

clickup_spec.feature: Task create — destination and type pickers
clickup_spec.behaviour: Before anything else the modal asks where the task lives and what it is. Location is required; the task cannot be created without a List.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Two pill dropdowns on the first row: left '⇄ <List name> ⌄' (destination picker: Space → List; opening it flips the chevron to '⌃'), right '◉ Task ⌄' (task-type picker, e.g. Task / Milestone). Both sit above the title field.

clickup_spec.feature: Inline Create List from the task flow
clickup_spec.behaviour: If the chosen Space has no List, the destination picker opens a 'Create List' dialog stacked over the task modal, so the user never leaves the create flow. Name is mandatory; privacy is decided at creation time.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Dialog title 'Create List'; row of AI/template suggestion chips ('Employee Onboarding & Management', 'Recruitment Pipeline', 'HR Goals & OKRs'); field label 'Name' with red '*'; input placeholder 'Your list or project name'; setting row 'Make private' with sub-label 'Only you and invited members have access' and a toggle (default OFF); primary 'Create' button, disabled until Name is non-empty; '✕' to close.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Immediately after a List is created, a second dialog offers to configure it. Each suggestion is an independently checkable card; the user can accept all or skip entirely and configure later.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Heading 'List settings'; subtitle 'Choose from our suggested settings or begin with a blank List.'; line 'AI Suggested settings for ☰ <list name>'. Cards, each with a checked purple checkbox: 'Default Task Type' → 'Task'; 'Default views' → 'List, Board'; 'Custom Fields' → 'Generating…' (async, purple); 'Statuses' → '○ Not Started → ◉ In Progress → ✔ Completed'. Buttons: 'No thanks' (ghost, left of primary) and 'Apply suggestions' (purple, muted until generation finishes).

clickup_spec.feature: Task create — name and rich description
clickup_spec.behaviour: Name and description live in the same modal. The description is a full document-grade editor: typing '/' opens a command palette that can insert blocks, mentions, live views and third-party embeds. The modal auto-grows when the description is focused.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Title placeholder "Task Name or type '/' for commands". Collapsed description prompt 'Add description, or write with ✨ AI'; focused description placeholder "Write or type '/' for commands and AI actions". Slash menu is two-column with section headers: TEXT (Checklist, Pull quote, Bulleted list, … scrolled), INLINE (Mention a Person, Mention a Page, Mention a Task, Mention a Whiteboard), VIEWS (ClickUp List (Table), ClickUp List (List), ClickUp List (Board)), EMBEDS (Embed website, GIPHY, CloudApp, Google Drive, +2 more). Inline hint line shows '/Type command…'.

clickup_spec.behaviour: All core task properties are settable before the task exists, as a row of chips that fill in with their value once set. An overflow '…' reveals the rest (time estimate, dependency, subtasks, checklist).
clickup_spec.ui_details: Empty state chips, in order: 'TO DO' (status), '⚙ Assignee', '📅 Due date', '⚑ Priority', '🏷 Tags', '…'. Filled state replaces the chip label with the value and adds a '✕' to clear, e.g. assignee becomes an avatar, date becomes '📅 Today, 7pm - 30/8/26, 9:15pm ✕', priority becomes '⚑ Urgent priority' with a red flag.

clickup_spec.feature: Date picker — start + due with presets, calendar and recurrence
clickup_spec.behaviour: One popover sets both start and due date. Natural-language presets, a month calendar, and a recurrence entry point all live in the same surface; picking a start then a due highlights the whole span on the calendar.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Two inputs at the top: '📅 Start date' and '📅 Due date', each with '✕' once set. Left preset column with right-aligned resolved values: 'Today — Fri', 'Later — 7:46 pm', 'Tomorrow — Sat', 'This weekend — Sat', 'Next week — Mon', 'Next weekend — 15 Aug', '2 weeks — 21 Aug', '4 weeks — 4 Sep', divider, 'Set Recurring ›'. Right calendar: 'August 2026' header, 'Today' button, up/down month chevrons, Mo–Su headers, today circled red, selected endpoints dark, the range between them shown as a highlighted band.

clickup_spec.behaviour: After a date is chosen the field offers a time. The time list is a scrollable dropdown in 15-minute increments; Enter accepts the highlighted entry. The chip then reads date + time for both ends.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Placeholder in the date field: 'Add time'. Dropdown entries '6:00 pm' … '10:15 pm' in 15-minute steps, first row highlighted with an 'Enter ⏎' affordance. Committed values render as 'Today at 7:00 pm' and '30/8/26 at 9:15 pm'; combined chip 'Today, 7pm - 30/8/26, 9:15pm'.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Tags are free-form and workspace-owned; the same input searches existing tags and creates a new one when you type a name and press Enter. Tagging is deliberately unconstrained ('YouTube-style').
clickup_spec.ui_details: Dropdown under the '🏷 Tags' chip: search input placeholder 'Search or add tags…', a section row 'Select an option' with a gear/settings icon on the right, and the empty state 'No tags created' in italic grey.

clickup_spec.behaviour: Priority is a four-level flag set from the chip row; the chip adopts the level's colour.
clickup_spec.ui_details: Selected value renders as '⚑ Urgent priority' with a red flag. Levels called out in the walkthrough: Urgent, High (plus the remaining levels).

clickup_spec.feature: Task create — custom fields and footer actions
